"""Synchronous SQLAlchemy engine and sessions shared by every service.

The agent graph, CRM, bookings and webhook guards are synchronous and run in
worker threads, so they share one pooled sync engine. PostgreSQL (Neon) is the
production database; outside production an unset ``DATABASE_URL`` falls back to
a local SQLite file so tests and local development need no server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from contextlib import contextmanager
from threading import Lock
from typing import Iterator

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, event, text
from sqlalchemy.engine import Engine
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool

from app.database.models import Base
from app.database.url import is_sqlite, redacted, sync_url
from app.helpers.config import get_settings


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

_engine: Engine | None = None
_factory: sessionmaker[Session] | None = None
_guard = Lock()


def _build_engine() -> Engine:
    settings = get_settings()
    url = sync_url(settings)

    if is_sqlite(url):
        in_memory = not url.database or url.database == ":memory:"
        engine = create_engine(
            url,
            connect_args={"check_same_thread": False},
            poolclass=StaticPool if in_memory else None,
            future=True,
        )

        @event.listens_for(engine, "connect")
        def _sqlite_pragmas(dbapi_connection, _record) -> None:  # pragma: no cover - driver hook
            cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
            cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
            if not in_memory:
                cursor.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
                cursor.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000")
            cursor.close()

        logger.info("Database: SQLite (%s) - development/test only", url.database or ":memory:")
        return engine

    engine = create_engine(
        url,
        pool_size=settings.DATABASE_POOL_SIZE,
        max_overflow=settings.DATABASE_MAX_OVERFLOW,
        pool_pre_ping=True,
        # Neon suspends idle computes after ~5 minutes and drops their sockets.
        pool_recycle=240,
        pool_timeout=15,
        connect_args={
            "connect_timeout": 10,
            # No server-side prepared statements: required behind a pooler
            # (pgbouncer transaction mode) and harmless otherwise.
            "prepare_threshold": None,
        },
        future=True,
    )
    logger.info("Database: PostgreSQL %s", redacted(url))
    return engine


def get_engine() -> Engine:
    global _engine, _factory
    if _engine is None:
        with _guard:
            if _engine is None:
                _engine = _build_engine()
                _factory = sessionmaker(bind=_engine, expire_on_commit=False, autoflush=False, future=True)
    return _engine


def reset_engine() -> None:
    """Dispose the engine so the next call rebuilds it from current settings."""
    global _engine, _factory
    with _guard:
        if _engine is not None:
            _engine.dispose()
        _engine = None
        _factory = None


def new_session() -> Session:
    get_engine()
    assert _factory is not None
    return _factory()


@contextmanager
def session_scope() -> Iterator[Session]:
    """A transaction: commits on success, rolls back on any error."""
    session = new_session()
    try:
        yield session
        session.commit()
    except Exception:
        session.rollback()
        raise
    finally:
        session.close()


def is_postgres() -> bool:
    return not is_sqlite(sync_url())


def create_all() -> None:
    """Create every table from the ORM models (SQLite dev/tests only).

    PostgreSQL schemas are managed exclusively by Alembic migrations.
    """
    engine = get_engine()
    if not is_sqlite(engine.url):
        raise RuntimeError("create_all() is for SQLite only; run `alembic upgrade head` for PostgreSQL")
    Base.metadata.create_all(engine)


def drop_all() -> None:
    engine = get_engine()
    if not is_sqlite(engine.url):
        raise RuntimeError("drop_all() is for SQLite only")
    Base.metadata.drop_all(engine)


def check_database() -> tuple[bool, str | None]:
    """Cheap connectivity probe for /health/ready (no secrets in the message)."""
    try:
        with get_engine().connect() as connection:
            connection.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        return True, None
    except Exception as error:
        return False, type(error).__name__

FILE: D:\ZaWolf\Real_estate-main\app\database\upsert.py
====================
"""Dialect-aware atomic insert helpers (PostgreSQL in production, SQLite in tests)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session


def insert_ignore(session: Session, model: type, values: dict[str, Any], index_elements: list[str]) -> bool:
    """``INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`` on PostgreSQL and SQLite.

    Atomic across workers, so two requests creating the same row never raise.
    Returns True when this call inserted the row, False when it already existed.

    The verdict comes from ``RETURNING``, not ``rowcount``: with psycopg 3 the
    row count of an INSERT is reported as -1, which would read as "inserted"
    every time and silently disable every caller's duplicate protection.
    """
    dialect = session.get_bind().dialect.name
    if dialect == "postgresql":
        from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert
    elif dialect == "sqlite":
        from sqlalchemy.dialects.sqlite import insert
    else:  # pragma: no cover - only the two supported databases
        raise RuntimeError(f"Unsupported database dialect: {dialect}")
    statement = (
        insert(model)
        .values(**values)
        .on_conflict_do_nothing(index_elements=index_elements)
        .returning(getattr(model, index_elements[0]))
    )
    return session.execute(statement).first() is not None

FILE: D:\ZaWolf\Real_estate-main\app\database\url.py

"""Build SQLAlchemy connection URLs from application settings.

One source of truth for the sync engine (services, LangGraph checkpointer,
Alembic) and the legacy async engine. Handles the details hosted PostgreSQL
(Neon) needs: percent-escaped credentials, ``postgres://`` URLs, mandatory TLS
for non-local hosts and driver-specific SSL parameters.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

from sqlalchemy.engine import URL, make_url

from app.helpers.config import Settings, get_settings


_LOCAL_HOSTS = {"localhost", "127.0.0.1", "::1", "postgres", "host.docker.internal"}
_DEV_SQLITE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "data" / "dev.sqlite3"


class DatabaseConfigError(RuntimeError):
    """The database is required but not (fully) configured."""


def _from_parts(settings: Settings) -> URL | None:
    if not settings.POSTGRES_HOST:
        return None
    missing = [
        name
        for name, value in (
            ("POSTGRES_USERNAME", settings.POSTGRES_USERNAME),
            ("POSTGRES_PASSWORD", settings.POSTGRES_PASSWORD),
            ("POSTGRES_PORT", settings.POSTGRES_PORT),
            ("POSTGRES_MAIN_DATABASE", settings.POSTGRES_MAIN_DATABASE),
        )
        if not value
    ]
    if missing:
        raise DatabaseConfigError("Missing PostgreSQL configuration: " + ", ".join(missing))
    # URL.create escapes special characters in the password.
    return URL.create(
        "postgresql",
        username=settings.POSTGRES_USERNAME,
        password=settings.POSTGRES_PASSWORD,
        host=settings.POSTGRES_HOST,
        port=settings.POSTGRES_PORT,
        database=settings.POSTGRES_MAIN_DATABASE,
    )


def configured_url(settings: Settings | None = None) -> URL | None:
    """The configured database URL, or None when nothing is configured."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    if settings.DATABASE_URL:
        try:
            return make_url(settings.DATABASE_URL)
        except Exception as error:  # ArgumentError carries the raw URL; do not echo it
            raise DatabaseConfigError("DATABASE_URL is not a valid database URL") from error
    return _from_parts(settings)


def resolve_url(settings: Settings | None = None) -> URL:
    """Return the URL to use, falling back to a local SQLite file outside production."""
    settings = settings or get_settings()
    url = configured_url(settings)
    if url is not None:
        return url
    if settings.is_production:
        raise DatabaseConfigError("DATABASE_URL (or POSTGRES_*) must be set in production")
    _DEV_SQLITE.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return URL.create("sqlite", database=str(_DEV_SQLITE))


def is_sqlite(url: URL) -> bool:
    return url.get_backend_name() == "sqlite"


def database_configured(settings: Settings | None = None) -> bool:
    return configured_url(settings) is not None


def sync_url(settings: Settings | None = None) -> URL:
    """URL for the synchronous psycopg (v3) driver."""
    url = resolve_url(settings)
    if is_sqlite(url):
        return url
    query = dict(url.query)
    if url.host not in _LOCAL_HOSTS:
        query.setdefault("sslmode", "require")
    return url.set(drivername="postgresql+psycopg", query=query)


def async_url(settings: Settings | None = None) -> URL:
    """URL for the asyncpg driver (legacy async repositories)."""
    url = resolve_url(settings)
    if is_sqlite(url):
        raise DatabaseConfigError("The async engine requires PostgreSQL")
    query = dict(url.query)
    sslmode = query.pop("sslmode", None)
    query.pop("channel_binding", None)
    if "ssl" not in query:
        if sslmode and sslmode != "disable":
            query["ssl"] = sslmode
        elif url.host not in _LOCAL_HOSTS:
            query["ssl"] = "require"
    return url.set(drivername="postgresql+asyncpg", query=query)


def libpq_conninfo(settings: Settings | None = None) -> str:
    """Connection string for plain psycopg (LangGraph checkpointer, advisory locks)."""
    url = sync_url(settings)
    if is_sqlite(url):
        raise DatabaseConfigError("A PostgreSQL connection string was requested but the database is SQLite")
    return url.set(drivername="postgresql").render_as_string(hide_password=False)


def redacted(url: URL) -> str:
    """Safe-to-log form of a URL (password masked)."""
    return url.render_as_string(hide_password=True)

"""Qdrant client and collection operations for RAG indexing."""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any, Iterable
from uuid import NAMESPACE_URL, uuid5

from qdrant_client import QdrantClient, models

from app.helpers.config import get_settings
from app.rag.embeddings import embedding_dimension


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Same default as Settings.QDRANT_COLLECTION, so code and .env agree.
DEFAULT_COLLECTION = "properties"

# Seconds before a Qdrant request is abandoned (cold free-tier clusters are slow).
QDRANT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 20


class VectorDimensionMismatch(RuntimeError):
    """The collection was built with a different embedding size than configured."""

_POINT_ID_NAMESPACE = NAMESPACE_URL

# Keep requests comfortably below Qdrant Cloud's 32 MB request limit.
UPSERT_BATCH_SIZE = 100


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Payload indexes
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Fields used by metadata filtering.
#
# Qdrant requires a payload index for filtered search. Keep the schema
# explicit so the collection has predictable filter behavior.
PAYLOAD_INDEXES: dict[str, models.PayloadSchemaType] = {
    "location": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "city": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "district": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "neighborhood": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "compound": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "property_type": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "transaction_type": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "developer": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "finishing": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "delivery": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "availability": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "currency": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "payment_plan": models.PayloadSchemaType.KEYWORD,
    "bedrooms": models.PayloadSchemaType.INTEGER,
    "bathrooms": models.PayloadSchemaType.INTEGER,
    "price": models.PayloadSchemaType.FLOAT,
    "area": models.PayloadSchemaType.FLOAT,
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Client
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def create_client(
    url: str | None = None,
    api_key: str | None = None,
) -> QdrantClient:
    """Create a Qdrant client from the application settings (``.env`` included)."""
    settings = get_settings()
    return QdrantClient(
        url=url or settings.qdrant_endpoint,
        api_key=api_key if api_key is not None else settings.QDRANT_API_KEY,
        timeout=QDRANT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
        # The client warns when its version differs from the cluster's; the
        # pinned range is verified against Qdrant Cloud.
        check_compatibility=False,
    )


def collection_vector_size(client: QdrantClient, collection_name: str) -> int | None:
    """Vector size of an existing collection, or None if it does not exist."""
    if not client.collection_exists(collection_name):
        return None
    vectors = client.get_collection(collection_name).config.params.vectors
    if isinstance(vectors, dict):  # named vectors: use the only/first one
        vectors = next(iter(vectors.values()), None)
    return getattr(vectors, "size", None)


def check_collection_dimension(client: QdrantClient, collection_name: str) -> None:
    """Fail loudly if the collection's vector size is not the configured one.

    Mixing embedding models silently ruins search quality (or Qdrant rejects the
    query with an opaque error), so this is checked before indexing and at
    readiness time.
    """
    size = collection_vector_size(client, collection_name)
    expected = embedding_dimension()
    if size is not None and size != expected:
        raise VectorDimensionMismatch(
            f"Collection '{collection_name}' has {size}-dimensional vectors but "
            f"EMBEDDING_DIMENSION={expected}. Re-index into a new collection "
            f"(scripts/ingest.py --rebuild) or set QDRANT_COLLECTION to a fresh name."
        )


def describe_collection() -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Readiness probe for /health/ready; never raises, never leaks credentials."""
    settings = get_settings()
    report: dict[str, Any] = {"ok": False, "collection": settings.QDRANT_COLLECTION, "expected_dimension": embedding_dimension()}
    client = None
    try:
        client = create_client()
        size = collection_vector_size(client, settings.QDRANT_COLLECTION)
        if size is None:
            report["error"] = "collection does not exist: run scripts/ingest.py"
        elif size != embedding_dimension():
            report.update(actual_dimension=size, error="vector size mismatch: re-index the collection")
        else:
            report.update(ok=True, actual_dimension=size, points=client.count(settings.QDRANT_COLLECTION, exact=False).count)
    except Exception as error:
        report["error"] = f"qdrant unreachable ({type(error).__name__})"
    finally:
        if client is not None:
            try:
                client.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
    return report


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def ensure_payload_indexes(
    client: QdrantClient,
    collection_name: str,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Ensure all metadata-filter fields have Qdrant payload indexes.

    Idempotent: indexes that already exist are skipped.
    Returns a dict mapping field name to one of:
        "created", "already_exists", "failed".
    """

    results: dict[str, str] = {}
    for field_name, schema_type in PAYLOAD_INDEXES.items():
        try:
            client.create_payload_index(
                collection_name=collection_name,
                field_name=field_name,
                field_schema=schema_type,
                wait=True,
            )
            results[field_name] = "created"
            logger.info("Payload index created | collection=%s field=%s", collection_name, field_name)
        except Exception as error:
            message = str(error)
            # Qdrant returns a 409 Conflict / "already exists" when the index
            # is already present; treat that as success.
            if "already exist" in message.lower() or "already exists" in message.lower():
                results[field_name] = "already_exists"
                logger.debug(
                    "Payload index already exists | collection=%s field=%s",
                    collection_name,
                    field_name,
                )
            else:
                results[field_name] = "failed"
                logger.exception(
                    "Payload index creation failed | collection=%s field=%s error=%s",
                    collection_name,
                    field_name,
                    error,
                )
    return results


def ensure_collection(
    client: QdrantClient,
    collection_name: str = DEFAULT_COLLECTION,
) -> None:
    """Ensure the collection and its metadata indexes exist."""

    if not client.collection_exists(collection_name):
        client.create_collection(
            collection_name=collection_name,
            vectors_config=models.VectorParams(
                size=embedding_dimension(),
                distance=models.Distance.COSINE,
            ),
        )
    else:
        check_collection_dimension(client, collection_name)

    index_results = ensure_payload_indexes(client, collection_name)
    created = [f for f, r in index_results.items() if r == "created"]
    skipped = [f for f, r in index_results.items() if r == "already_exists"]
    failed = [f for f, r in index_results.items() if r == "failed"]
    if created:
        logger.info(
            "Payload indexes created | collection=%s indexes=%s",
            collection_name,
            ", ".join(created),
        )
    if skipped:
        logger.debug(
            "Payload indexes already exist | collection=%s indexes=%s",
            collection_name,
            ", ".join(skipped),
        )
    if failed:
        logger.warning(
            "Payload indexes failed | collection=%s indexes=%s",
            collection_name,
            ", ".join(failed),
        )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Upsert
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def upsert_chunks(
    client: QdrantClient,
    collection_name: str,
    chunks: Iterable[dict[str, Any]],
    vectors: Iterable[list[float]],
) -> int:
    """Upsert embedded chunks in batches with searchable metadata payloads."""

    chunk_list = list(chunks)
    vector_list = list(vectors)

    if len(chunk_list) != len(vector_list):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Chunk/vector count mismatch: {len(chunk_list)} chunks, "
            f"{len(vector_list)} vectors"
        )

    points: list[models.PointStruct] = []

    for chunk, vector in zip(chunk_list, vector_list):
        chunk_id = str(chunk.get("id") or chunk.get("chunk_id") or "")

        if not chunk_id:
            raise ValueError("Each chunk must include a deterministic id")

        metadata = chunk.get("metadata") or {}

        if not isinstance(metadata, dict):
            raise TypeError("Chunk metadata must be a dictionary")

        if len(vector) != embedding_dimension():
            raise ValueError(
                f"Expected {embedding_dimension()}-dimensional vector, "
                f"got {len(vector)}"
            )

        payload = {
            **metadata,
            "text": chunk.get("text", ""),
            "id": chunk_id,
            "chunk_id": chunk_id,
            "metadata": metadata,
        }

        # Qdrant accepts unsigned integers or UUIDs as point IDs.
        # Derive a stable UUID from the original chunk ID so arbitrary
        # deterministic IDs remain repeatable across indexing runs.
        point_id = str(uuid5(_POINT_ID_NAMESPACE, chunk_id))

        points.append(
            models.PointStruct(
                id=point_id,
                vector=vector,
                payload=payload,
            )
        )

    if not points:
        return 0

    total = 0

    for start in range(0, len(points), UPSERT_BATCH_SIZE):
        batch = points[start : start + UPSERT_BATCH_SIZE]

        client.upsert(
            collection_name=collection_name,
            points=batch,
            wait=True,
        )

        total += len(batch)

    return total


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Collection lifecycle
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def delete_collection(
    client: QdrantClient,
    collection_name: str,
) -> None:
    """Delete a collection if it exists."""

    if client.collection_exists(collection_name):
        client.delete_collection(collection_name)


def rebuild_collection(
    client: QdrantClient,
    collection_name: str = DEFAULT_COLLECTION,
) -> None:
    """Drop and recreate a collection with the configured schema."""

    delete_collection(client, collection_name)
    ensure_collection(client, collection_name)

            channels.append("telegram")
        if self.STAFF_WHATSAPP_NUMBER and self.whatsapp_configured:
            channels.append("whatsapp")
        if self.SMTP_HOST and self.SMTP_FROM and self.STAFF_EMAIL_TO:
            channels.append("email")

    def production_problems(self) -> list[str]:
        """Return human-readable configuration errors; never includes secret values.

        An empty list means the process is safe to start with APP_ENV=production.
        """
        problems: list[str] = []

        def missing(name: str, why: str) -> None:
            problems.append(f"{name} is required: {why}")

        if not (self.DATABASE_URL or self.POSTGRES_HOST):
            missing("DATABASE_URL", "conversations, CRM and bookings are stored in PostgreSQL")
        if not self.SESSION_SECRET or len(self.SESSION_SECRET) < 32:
            missing("SESSION_SECRET", "at least 32 characters; signs website sessions and voice tokens")
        if not self.ADMIN_API_KEY or len(self.ADMIN_API_KEY) < 24:
            missing("ADMIN_API_KEY", "at least 24 characters; staff confirm bookings and handoffs with it")

        origins = self.cors_origins
        if not origins or "*" in origins:
            problems.append("CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS must list the real frontend origin(s), not '*'")
        else:
            for origin in origins:
                parsed = urlparse(origin)
                if parsed.scheme != "https" and parsed.hostname not in {"localhost", "127.0.0.1"}:
                    problems.append(f"CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS entry {origin!r} must use https")

        if not self.GROQ_API_KEY:
            missing("GROQ_API_KEY", "grounded answer generation and the reranker")
        if self.EMBEDDING_BACKEND == "gemini" and not self.GEMINI_API_KEY:
            missing("GEMINI_API_KEY", "query/document embeddings (EMBEDDING_BACKEND=gemini)")

        qdrant_host = urlparse(self.qdrant_endpoint).hostname or ""
        if qdrant_host in _LOCAL_HOSTS:
            missing("QDRANT_URL", "point it at Qdrant Cloud, not a local instance")
        elif not self.QDRANT_API_KEY:
            missing("QDRANT_API_KEY", "Qdrant Cloud requires an API key")

        whatsapp_parts = {
            "WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN": self.WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN,
            "WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET": self.WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET,
            "WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN": self.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN,
            "WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID": self.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID,
        }
        if any(whatsapp_parts.values()):
            for name, value in whatsapp_parts.items():
                if not value:
                    missing(name, "WhatsApp is partially configured; set all four WHATSAPP_* values or none")

        if self.RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED and self.TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS < 1:
            problems.append(
                "TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS must be >= 1 behind Render's proxy, otherwise every client shares one rate-limit bucket"
            )
        return problems

    def production_warnings(self) -> list[str]:
        """Non-fatal gaps worth surfacing in the startup log."""
        warnings: list[str] = []
        if not self.GEMINI_API_KEY:
            warnings.append("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set: voice chat is disabled")
        if not self.staff_channels:
            warnings.append("no staff notification channel configured: booking/handoff alerts only reach the admin API")
        if not self.whatsapp_configured:
            warnings.append("WhatsApp is not configured: the WhatsApp channel is disabled")
        if self.SHOW_DEMO_LISTINGS:
            warnings.append("SHOW_DEMO_LISTINGS is on: test listings are shown to visitors, labelled as demo data")
        return warnings


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    """Return one cached settings instance for the process."""
    return Settings()


def reset_settings_cache() -> None:
    """Drop the cached settings (tests that change environment variables)."""
    get_settings.cache_clear()

"""Phone-number normalisation, validation and presentation.

Numbers reach the assistant as typed text, speech-to-text output (Arabic-Indic
digits, spaces between digits) and WhatsApp sender ids (digits, no ``+``). Every
path normalises to E.164 here, so the same customer always has the same string
and a booking can never be created for a number we could not parse.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re


_DIGIT_TABLE = str.maketrans("Ù Ù¡Ù¢Ù£Ù¤Ù¥Ù¦Ù§Ù¨Ù©Û°Û±Û²Û³Û´ÛµÛ¶Û·Û¸Û¹", "01234567890123456789")

# Egyptian mobile operators: 010 Vodafone, 011 Etisalat, 012 Orange, 015 WE.
_EG_LOCAL = re.compile(r"^01[0125]\d{8}$")
_EG_INTERNATIONAL = re.compile(r"^201[0125]\d{8}$")


def normalize_phone(raw: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Return the number in E.164 form (``+201012345678``) or None if invalid.

    Accepts Egyptian local format (``01012345678``), international with or
    without ``+``/``00``, and any other international number of 8-15 digits that
    starts with ``+``/``00``. Anything else (too short, letters, a bare local
    number from another country) is rejected rather than guessed.
    """
    if not raw:
        return None
    text = str(raw).translate(_DIGIT_TABLE).strip()
    # Only digits and common separators are allowed; "0101abc" is not a number.
    if re.search(r"[^\d+\s().\-]", text) or text.count("+") > 1 or ("+" in text and not text.startswith("+")):
        return None
    has_plus = text.startswith("+")
    digits = re.sub(r"\D", "", text)
    if not digits:
        return None

    if not has_plus and digits.startswith("00"):
        digits, has_plus = digits[2:], True

    if not has_plus:
        if _EG_LOCAL.match(digits):
            return "+20" + digits[1:]
        if _EG_INTERNATIONAL.match(digits):
            return "+" + digits
        return None

    if digits.startswith("20"):
        return "+" + digits if _EG_INTERNATIONAL.match(digits) else None
    if 8 <= len(digits) <= 15 and digits[0] != "0":
        return "+" + digits
    return None


def is_valid_phone(raw: str | None) -> bool:
    return normalize_phone(raw) is not None


def mask_phone(phone: str | None) -> str:
    """Log-safe form: keeps the country prefix and the last two digits."""
    value = normalize_phone(phone) or str(phone or "")
    if len(value) <= 6:
        return "***"
    return f"{value[:4]}{'*' * (len(value) - 6)}{value[-2:]}"


def display_phone(phone: str) -> str:
    """Human-readable form for reading back to the customer (``0101 234 5678``)."""
    value = normalize_phone(phone) or phone
    if value.startswith("+20") and len(value) == 13:
        local = "0" + value[3:]
        return f"{local[:4]} {local[4:7]} {local[7:]}"
    return value


def spoken_phone(phone: str) -> str:
    """Digit-by-digit form for voice read-back, so speech never merges digits."""
    value = normalize_phone(phone) or phone
    if value.startswith("+20") and len(value) == 13:
        value = "0" + value[3:]
    return " ".join(value.lstrip("+"))

"""Rules for escalating a conversation to a human sales representative."""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Mapping

from app.leads.scoring import calculate_lead_score


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HandoffDecision:
    required: bool
    reason: str | None = None
    priority: str = "normal"


def evaluate_handoff(context: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> HandoffDecision:
    """Return a handoff decision for explicit requests, risk, or high intent."""
    data = context or {}
    if data.get("requested_human"):
        return HandoffDecision(True, "customer_requested_human", "high")
    if data.get("complaint") or data.get("legal_or_financial_risk"):
        return HandoffDecision(True, "sensitive_request", "high")
    if data.get("requested_viewing") and calculate_lead_score(data) >= 70:
        return HandoffDecision(True, "high_intent_lead", "high")
    return HandoffDecision(False)

"""Lead qualification helpers shared by agents and API services."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any


REQUIRED_QUALIFICATION_FIELDS = ("budget", "purpose", "timeline")


def missing_qualification_fields(
    qualification: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Return required fields that have no meaningful value."""
    values = qualification or {}
    return [
        field
        for field in REQUIRED_QUALIFICATION_FIELDS
        if values.get(field) is None or values.get(field) == ""
    ]


def is_qualified(qualification: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> bool:
    """Return whether the minimum sales-qualification data is present."""
    return not missing_qualification_fields(qualification)

FILE: D:\ZaWolf\Real_estate-main\app\leads\scoring.py
====================
"""Deterministic lead scoring for the real-estate sales workflow."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any


def calculate_lead_score(signals: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> int:
    """Calculate a transparent 0â€“100 score from common qualification signals."""
    data = signals or {}
    score = 0

    if data.get("budget") not in (None, "", 0):
        score += 25
    if data.get("purpose") not in (None, ""):
        score += 15
    if data.get("timeline") not in (None, ""):
        score += 20
    if data.get("preferred_location") or data.get("location"):
        score += 10
    if data.get("property_type"):
        score += 10
    if data.get("financing_ready") is True:
        score += 10
    if data.get("requested_viewing") is True:
        score += 10

    return min(score, 100)


def score_band(score: int) -> str:
    """Map a numeric score to an operational priority band."""
    if not 0 <= score <= 100:
        raise ValueError("score must be between 0 and 100")
    if score >= 70:
        return "hot"
    if score >= 40:
        return "warm"
    return "cold"

from typing import TypeVar
from app.llm.prompts import SYSTEM_PROMPT
from groq import Groq
from pydantic import BaseModel
from app.helpers.config import get_settings


T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)


class LLMClient:
    def __init__(
        self,
        api_key: str | None = None,
        model: str | None = None,
    ):
        settings = get_settings()
        configured_api_key = api_key or settings.GROQ_API_KEY
        if not configured_api_key:
            raise RuntimeError("GROQ_API_KEY is not configured.")
        self.client = Groq(api_key=configured_api_key)
        self.model = model or settings.GENERATION_MODEL or settings.GROQ_MODEL

    def generate(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        system_prompt: str = SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    ) -> str:
        messages = []

        if system_prompt:
            messages.append({
                "role": "system",
                "content": system_prompt,
            })

        messages.append({
            "role": "user",
            "content": prompt,
        })

        return self.generate_messages(messages)

    def generate_messages(
        self,
        messages: list[dict[str, str]],
        temperature: float | None = None,
        max_tokens: int | None = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Generate from an explicit conversation message list."""
        if not messages:
            raise ValueError("At least one message is required for generation.")

        request = {
            "model": self.model,
            "messages": messages,
        }
        if temperature is not None:
            request["temperature"] = temperature
        if max_tokens is not None:
            request["max_tokens"] = max_tokens

        response = self.client.chat.completions.create(**request)
        if not response.choices:
            raise ValueError("LLM returned no completion choices.")
        return response.choices[0].message.content or ""

    def generate_structured(
        self,
        prompt: str,
        output_schema: type[T],
        system_prompt: str = SYSTEM_PROMPT,
    ) -> T:
        messages = []

        if system_prompt:
            messages.append({
                "role": "system",
                "content": system_prompt,
            })

        messages.append({
            "role": "user",
            "content": prompt,
        })

        response = self.client.chat.completions.parse(
            model=self.model,
            messages=messages,
            response_format=output_schema,
        )

        parsed = response.choices[0].message.parsed

        if parsed is None:
            raise ValueError(
                "LLM returned no structured output."
            )

        return parsed

"""Proactive messages to customers (booking confirmed / cancelled by staff).

Only WhatsApp customers can be reached this way: a website visitor has no push
channel, so they see the new status when they return to the chat or when the
advisor phones them. Meta only allows free-form messages inside the 24-hour
window after the customer last wrote; outside it the send is rejected and we
log the failure rather than pretend it worked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging

import httpx

from app.helpers.config import get_settings
from app.helpers.phone import mask_phone


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def send_to_customer(external_id: str, text: str) -> bool:
    """Deliver ``text`` to the customer's channel. Returns True if sent."""
    channel, _, address = external_id.partition(":")
    settings = get_settings()
    if channel != "whatsapp" or not address:
        logger.info("Customer %s has no push channel; notice not sent", channel)
        return False
    if not (settings.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN and settings.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID):
        logger.warning("WhatsApp sending is not configured; customer notice not sent")
        return False
    try:
        response = httpx.post(
            f"https://graph.facebook.com/{settings.WHATSAPP_API_VERSION}/{settings.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages",
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {settings.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN}"},
            json={
                "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
                "to": "".join(ch for ch in address if ch.isdigit()),
                "type": "text",
                "text": {"body": text[:4096]},
            },
            timeout=httpx.Timeout(15.0),
        )
        response.raise_for_status()
        return True
    except Exception as error:
        status = error.response.status_code if isinstance(error, httpx.HTTPStatusError) else type(error).__name__
        logger.warning("WhatsApp customer notice to %s failed: %s", mask_phone(address), status)
        return False

"""Staff notifications with a durable outbox.

Every alert is stored in ``staff_notifications`` before any delivery is tried, so
it is visible through the admin API and can be retried even when every provider
is down. Delivery fans out to each configured channel (webhook, Telegram,
WhatsApp, e-mail); an alert counts as sent when at least one channel accepts it.

Nothing here may raise into a customer request: a failed alert must never turn a
successful booking into an error.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import smtplib
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from email.message import EmailMessage
from typing import Any, Callable

import httpx
from sqlalchemy import select

from app.database import models as db
from app.database.session import session_scope
from app.helpers.config import get_settings


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS = 3_500
_TIMEOUT = httpx.Timeout(10.0)


def _describe_error(error: Exception) -> str:
    """Error text that is safe to store and log.

    httpx puts the full request URL in its messages, and Telegram's URL carries
    the bot token, so only the exception class and HTTP status are kept.
    """
    if isinstance(error, httpx.HTTPStatusError):
        return f"HTTP {error.response.status_code}"
    return type(error).__name__


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Channels: each takes the message text and raises on failure
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _send_webhook(message: str) -> None:
    url = get_settings().STAFF_WEBHOOK_URL
    # "text" is Slack/Mattermost's field, "content" is Discord's.
    response = httpx.post(url, json={"text": message, "content": message}, timeout=_TIMEOUT)
    response.raise_for_status()


def _send_telegram(message: str) -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    response = httpx.post(
        f"https://api.telegram.org/bot{settings.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}/sendMessage",
        json={"chat_id": settings.TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, "text": message, "disable_web_page_preview": True},
        timeout=_TIMEOUT,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()


def _send_whatsapp(message: str) -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    response = httpx.post(
        f"https://graph.facebook.com/{settings.WHATSAPP_API_VERSION}/{settings.WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID}/messages",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {settings.WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN}"},
        json={
            "messaging_product": "whatsapp",
            "to": "".join(ch for ch in settings.STAFF_WHATSAPP_NUMBER if ch.isdigit()),
            "type": "text",
            "text": {"body": message[:4096]},
        },
        timeout=_TIMEOUT,
    )
    response.raise_for_status()


def _send_email(message: str) -> None:
    settings = get_settings()
    email = EmailMessage()
    email["From"] = settings.SMTP_FROM
    email["To"] = settings.STAFF_EMAIL_TO
    email["Subject"] = message.splitlines()[0][:120] if message else "Aqar alert"
    email.set_content(message)
    with smtplib.SMTP(settings.SMTP_HOST, settings.SMTP_PORT, timeout=10) as smtp:
        smtp.starttls()
        if settings.SMTP_USERNAME and settings.SMTP_PASSWORD:
            smtp.login(settings.SMTP_USERNAME, settings.SMTP_PASSWORD)
        smtp.send_message(email)


_CHANNELS: dict[str, Callable[[str], None]] = {
    "webhook": _send_webhook,
    "telegram": _send_telegram,
    "whatsapp": _send_whatsapp,
    "email": _send_email,
}


def _deliver(message: str) -> tuple[bool, str | None, bool]:
    """Try every configured channel. Returns (any_sent, error_summary, had_channels)."""
    channels = get_settings().staff_channels
    if not channels:
        return False, None, False
    errors: list[str] = []
    sent = False
    for name in channels:
        try:
            _CHANNELS[name](message)
            sent = True
        except Exception as error:
            errors.append(f"{name}: {_describe_error(error)}")
            logger.warning("Staff notification via %s failed: %s", name, _describe_error(error))
    return sent, "; ".join(errors) or None, True


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Public API
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _attempt(notification_id: int) -> str:
    """Deliver one stored notification and record the outcome."""
    with session_scope() as session:
        row = session.get(db.StaffNotification, notification_id)
        if row is None or row.status == "sent":
            return "missing" if row is None else "sent"
        sent, error, had_channels = _deliver(row.message)
        row.attempts += 1
        if sent:
            row.status, row.sent_at, row.last_error = "sent", datetime.now(timezone.utc), error
        elif not had_channels:
            row.status = "no_channel"
        else:
            row.status = "failed" if row.attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS else "abandoned"
            row.last_error = error
        return row.status


def notify_staff(
    kind: str,
    message: str,
    *,
    ref_type: str | None = None,
    ref_id: str | None = None,
    payload: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> int | None:
    """Store an alert and try to deliver it. Never raises; returns the outbox id."""
    try:
        with session_scope() as session:
            row = db.StaffNotification(
                kind=kind,
                ref_type=ref_type,
                ref_id=ref_id,
                message=message[:MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS],
                payload=payload,
                status="pending",
                attempts=0,
            )
            session.add(row)
            session.flush()
            notification_id = row.id
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Could not store staff notification | kind=%s", kind)
        return None
    try:
        _attempt(notification_id)
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Staff notification delivery crashed | id=%s", notification_id)
    return notification_id


def retry_pending(limit: int = 20) -> int:
    """Retry undelivered alerts (failed, or stored while no channel existed)."""
    if not get_settings().staff_channels:
        return 0
    try:
        with session_scope() as session:
            ids = list(
                session.scalars(
                    select(db.StaffNotification.id)
                    .where(db.StaffNotification.status.in_(("pending", "failed", "no_channel")))
                    .order_by(db.StaffNotification.id)
                    .limit(limit)
                )
            )
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("Could not list pending staff notifications")
        return 0
    delivered = 0
    for notification_id in ids:
        try:
            if _attempt(notification_id) == "sent":
                delivered += 1
        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Staff notification retry crashed | id=%s", notification_id)
    return delivered

"""Application logging: structured, request-correlated and secret-free."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
import re
import sys
from contextvars import ContextVar
from datetime import datetime, timezone

# Set per request by the middleware in app.main; shows up on every log line.
request_id_var: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar("request_id", default=None)

# Last line of defence: scrub anything that looks like a credential before it is
# written, in case a library logs a URL or header it should not.
_REDACTIONS = (
    (re.compile(r"(?i)(token|api[_-]?key|secret|password|authorization|x-admin-key)(=|:\s*|\"\s*:\s*\")([^\s&\"',;]+)"), r"\1\2[redacted]"),
    (re.compile(r"(?i)bearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._\-]+"), "Bearer [redacted]"),
    (re.compile(r"\bgsk_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}"), "[redacted-groq-key]"),
    (re.compile(r"\bAIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{20,}"), "[redacted-google-key]"),
    (re.compile(r"\bEAA[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}"), "[redacted-meta-token]"),
    (re.compile(r"/bot\d+:[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}"), "/bot[redacted]"),
    (re.compile(r"postgres(?:ql)?(?:\+\w+)?://[^\s:@/]+:[^\s@]+@"), "postgresql://[redacted]@"),
)


def redact(text: str) -> str:
    for pattern, replacement in _REDACTIONS:
        text = pattern.sub(replacement, text)
    return text


class RedactingFilter(logging.Filter):
    def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool:
        try:
            message = record.getMessage()
        except Exception:
            return True
        scrubbed = redact(message)
        if scrubbed != message:
            record.msg, record.args = scrubbed, None
        if record.exc_info and record.exc_info[1] is not None:
            record.exc_text = redact(logging.Formatter().formatException(record.exc_info))
        return True


class JsonFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        payload = {
            "ts": datetime.fromtimestamp(record.created, timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="milliseconds"),
            "level": record.levelname,
            "logger": record.name,
            "message": record.getMessage(),
        }
        request_id = request_id_var.get()
        if request_id:
            payload["request_id"] = request_id
        if record.exc_info:
            payload["exception"] = record.exc_text or redact(self.formatException(record.exc_info))
        return json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)


class _TextFormatter(logging.Formatter):
    def format(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> str:
        request_id = request_id_var.get()
        base = super().format(record)
        return f"{base} [req={request_id}]" if request_id else base


# Libraries that log full URLs / payloads at INFO.
_QUIET_LOGGERS = ("httpx", "httpcore", "urllib3", "google_genai", "google.genai", "websockets", "qdrant_client", "groq", "uvicorn.access")


def configure_logging(level: str | int | None = None, fmt: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Configure process-wide logging (idempotent)."""
    from app.helpers.config import get_settings

    settings = get_settings()
    handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout)
    handler.addFilter(RedactingFilter())
    use_json = (fmt or settings.LOG_FORMAT) == "json"
    handler.setFormatter(
        JsonFormatter() if use_json else _TextFormatter("%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    )

    root = logging.getLogger()
    root.handlers[:] = [handler]
    root.setLevel(level or settings.LOG_LEVEL)

    for name in _QUIET_LOGGERS:
        logging.getLogger(name).setLevel(logging.WARNING)

    # uvicorn logs rejected/accepted WebSocket upgrades (with the query string, i.e.
    # the single-use voice token) through its own handler, which bypasses the filter
    # above. Filter at the logger so those lines are scrubbed too.
    for name in ("uvicorn", "uvicorn.error"):
        uvicorn_logger = logging.getLogger(name)
        if not any(isinstance(f, RedactingFilter) for f in uvicorn_logger.filters):
            uvicorn_logger.addFilter(RedactingFilter())

"""Small dependency-free tracing context for logs and diagnostics."""

from __future__ import annotations

from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from collections.abc import Iterator
from uuid import uuid4


trace_id_context: ContextVar[str | None] = ContextVar("trace_id", default=None)


def current_trace_id() -> str | None:
    return trace_id_context.get()


@contextmanager
def trace(trace_id: str | None = None) -> Iterator[str]:
    value = trace_id or str(uuid4())
    token = trace_id_context.set(value)
    try:
        yield value
    finally:
        trace_id_context.reset(token)

"""
floorplan_parser.py

Parses floor plans / unit sketches for *structural* information:
room layout, room count, approximate room boundaries, and overall
shape â€” complementary to OCR, which pulls labels/numbers (e.g. "3.2m",
"Bedroom 1") from the same image.

Per the project's AI design principles, this module only extracts
structured signals â€” it does not decide property attributes on its
own. Its output should be combined with OCR text and reconciled by
`app/rag/normalization/` before it's treated as trusted property data.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List, Optional, Tuple, Union
from pathlib import Path

import cv2
import numpy as np

from .image_processor import preprocess_image, ImagePreprocessConfig


@dataclass
class RoomRegion:
    """A detected room-like region within the floor plan image."""
    label: Optional[str] = None          # filled in later by OCR/normalization, if available
    bounding_box: Tuple[int, int, int, int] = (0, 0, 0, 0)  # x, y, w, h in pixels
    area_px: float = 0.0
    approx_shape: str = "unknown"        # "rectangular" | "irregular"


@dataclass
class FloorplanResult:
    source_file: str
    room_count_estimate: int = 0
    regions: List[RoomRegion] = field(default_factory=list)
    image_size: Tuple[int, int] = (0, 0)  # width, height
    confidence: float = 0.0
    notes: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)


def _detect_room_regions(gray: np.ndarray) -> List[RoomRegion]:
    """Heuristic wall/room segmentation: threshold + contour detection.

    This is a lightweight geometric baseline suitable for clean, mostly
    line-based floor plans. For noisy/hand-drawn sketches or complex
    architectural drawings, replace this with a trained segmentation
    model (e.g. a U-Net style room-layout model) behind the same
    interface â€” the rest of the pipeline doesn't need to change.
    """
    blurred = cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0)
    edges = cv2.Canny(blurred, 50, 150)
    dilated = cv2.dilate(edges, np.ones((3, 3), np.uint8), iterations=2)

    contours, _ = cv2.findContours(
        dilated, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE
    )

    image_area = gray.shape[0] * gray.shape[1]
    regions: List[RoomRegion] = []

    for cnt in contours:
        area = cv2.contourArea(cnt)
        # Filter out noise and the full-page outer contour.
        if area < image_area * 0.01 or area > image_area * 0.9:
            continue

        x, y, w, h = cv2.boundingRect(cnt)
        perimeter = cv2.arcLength(cnt, True)
        approx = cv2.approxPolyDP(cnt, 0.02 * perimeter, True)
        shape = "rectangular" if len(approx) == 4 else "irregular"

        regions.append(RoomRegion(
            bounding_box=(x, y, w, h),
            area_px=area,
            approx_shape=shape,
        ))

    return regions


def parse_floorplan(
    source: Union[str, Path, bytes, np.ndarray],
    source_file: Optional[str] = None,
    preprocess_config: Optional[ImagePreprocessConfig] = None,
) -> FloorplanResult:
    """Extract structural layout information from a floor plan / unit
    sketch image.
    """
    # Floor plans benefit from deskew + grayscale before edge detection.
    config = preprocess_config or ImagePreprocessConfig(
        deskew=True, denoise=True, to_grayscale=True,
    )
    img = preprocess_image(source, config)
    gray = img if img.ndim == 2 else cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    regions = _detect_room_regions(gray)

    notes = []
    if not regions:
        notes.append(
            "No room regions detected â€” image may be low quality, "
            "hand-drawn, or not a standard floor plan layout."
        )

    confidence = min(1.0, len(regions) / 6.0) if regions else 0.0

    return FloorplanResult(
        source_file=source_file or (str(source) if isinstance(source, (str, Path)) else "in_memory"),
        room_count_estimate=len(regions),
        regions=regions,
        image_size=(gray.shape[1], gray.shape[0]),
        confidence=confidence,
        notes=notes,
    )

"""
image_processor.py

Shared, low-level image preprocessing used by both `vision_extractor`
(property photos) and `floorplan_parser` (floor plans / unit sketches)
before either is fed to OCR or a CV model.

Kept dependency-light: OpenCV + Pillow only. No ML models here.
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Optional, Union

import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image


@dataclass
class ImagePreprocessConfig:
    """Tunable preprocessing options.

    max_dimension: downscale so the longer side never exceeds this
        (keeps CV/OCR calls fast and cost-predictable).
    denoise: apply light denoising â€” helps scanned/low-quality uploads.
    deskew: attempt automatic rotation correction (useful for scanned
        contracts / floor plans photographed at an angle).
    to_grayscale: convert to grayscale (usually only wanted before OCR,
        NOT before a vision model that needs color/layout cues).
    """
    max_dimension: int = 2000
    denoise: bool = True
    deskew: bool = True
    to_grayscale: bool = False


def load_image(source: Union[str, Path, bytes, np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Load an image from a path, raw bytes, or an existing array into a
    BGR numpy array (OpenCV convention).
    """
    if isinstance(source, np.ndarray):
        return source

    if isinstance(source, (str, Path)):
        img = cv2.imread(str(source), cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        if img is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Could not read image at path: {source}")
        return img

    if isinstance(source, bytes):
        arr = np.frombuffer(source, dtype=np.uint8)
        img = cv2.imdecode(arr, cv2.IMREAD_COLOR)
        if img is None:
            raise ValueError("Could not decode image from bytes")
        return img

    raise TypeError(f"Unsupported image source type: {type(source)}")


def _resize_if_needed(img: np.ndarray, max_dimension: int) -> np.ndarray:
    h, w = img.shape[:2]
    longest = max(h, w)
    if longest <= max_dimension:
        return img
    scale = max_dimension / float(longest)
    new_size = (int(w * scale), int(h * scale))
    return cv2.resize(img, new_size, interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)


def _denoise(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return cv2.fastNlMeansDenoisingColored(img, None, 5, 5, 7, 21)


def _deskew(img: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Estimate skew angle from the largest text/line contours and rotate
    to correct it. Conservative: only rotates for small angles typical of
    scanned documents / photographed floor plans, not general photos.
    """
    gray = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
    gray = cv2.bitwise_not(gray)
    thresh = cv2.threshold(gray, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY | cv2.THRESH_OTSU)[1]

    coords = np.column_stack(np.where(thresh > 0))
    if coords.shape[0] < 50:
        return img  # not enough signal to estimate skew reliably

    angle = cv2.minAreaRect(coords)[-1]
    if angle < -45:
        angle = -(90 + angle)
    else:
        angle = -angle

    if abs(angle) < 0.5 or abs(angle) > 15:
        return img  # ignore negligible or implausible angles

    (h, w) = img.shape[:2]
    center = (w // 2, h // 2)
    matrix = cv2.getRotationMatrix2D(center, angle, 1.0)
    return cv2.warpAffine(
        img, matrix, (w, h),
        flags=cv2.INTER_CUBIC, borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE,
    )


def preprocess_image(
    source: Union[str, Path, bytes, np.ndarray],
    config: Optional[ImagePreprocessConfig] = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Run the standard preprocessing pipeline and return a BGR numpy array
    ready for OCR or a vision model.
    """
    config = config or ImagePreprocessConfig()
    img = load_image(source)
    img = _resize_if_needed(img, config.max_dimension)

    if config.deskew:
        img = _deskew(img)
    if config.denoise:
        img = _denoise(img)
    if config.to_grayscale:
        img = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

    return img


def to_pil(img: np.ndarray) -> Image.Image:
    """Convert a BGR (or grayscale) numpy array to a PIL Image (RGB),
    for handing off to libraries/APIs that expect PIL/RGB input.
    """
    if img.ndim == 2:
        return Image.fromarray(img)
    rgb = cv2.cvtColor(img, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
    return Image.fromarray(rgb)

"""
vision_extractor.py

Extracts *visual* information from general property photos (interiors,
exteriors, amenities) â€” room type, condition/quality cues, and a
description usable for embeddings / search.

This does NOT read text (that's `app/rag/ocr/`) and does NOT parse
structural floor-plan layouts (that's `floorplan_parser.py`).

Backend: fully open-source, runs locally via `transformers`.
  - Captioning: Salesforce BLIP (image-to-text)
  - Attributes (room_type / condition / style / amenities): CLIP
    zero-shot classification against candidate label lists â€” no
    training needed, just a labeled vocabulary you control.

Models load once (lazily, on first call) and are cached in the module.
Swap MODEL_NAMES below to try other open checkpoints (e.g. a LLaVA
variant for richer captions) without touching the rest of the file.

Install:
    pip install transformers torch pillow
"""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Union
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np

from .image_processor import preprocess_image, to_pil, ImagePreprocessConfig


@dataclass
class VisualFeatures:
    """Normalized output of visual extraction for one property image."""
    source_file: str
    room_type: Optional[str] = None          # e.g. "living_room", "kitchen", "bedroom", "exterior"
    condition: Optional[str] = None          # e.g. "new", "good", "needs_renovation"
    style_tags: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)   # e.g. ["modern", "furnished"]
    detected_amenities: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # e.g. ["pool", "balcony"]
    caption: Optional[str] = None            # natural-language description, embeddable
    confidence: float = 0.0
    raw_model_output: Optional[dict] = None  # kept for traceability / debugging


MODEL_NAMES = {
    "caption": "Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-base",
    "clip": "openai/clip-vit-base-patch32",
}

# Candidate label vocabularies for CLIP zero-shot classification.
# Edit these to match your actual property taxonomy / CRM fields.
ROOM_TYPE_LABELS = [
    "living room", "bedroom", "kitchen", "bathroom",
    "dining room", "balcony", "building exterior", "swimming pool area",
]
CONDITION_LABELS = ["new / like new", "good condition", "needs renovation"]
STYLE_LABELS = ["modern", "classic", "minimalist", "luxurious", "furnished", "unfurnished"]
AMENITY_LABELS = [
    "swimming pool", "garden", "balcony", "parking garage",
    "elevator", "gym", "security gate", "sea view",
]

# CLIP similarity threshold above which a style/amenity tag is kept
# (style_tags and amenities can have multiple hits; room_type/condition
# always take the single best match).
_TAG_THRESHOLD = 0.22

_models: Dict[str, object] = {}


def _get_models():
    """Lazily load and cache the BLIP + CLIP models/processors."""
    if _models:
        return _models

    import torch
    from transformers import (
        BlipProcessor, BlipForConditionalGeneration,
        CLIPProcessor, CLIPModel,
    )

    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

    blip_processor = BlipProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAMES["caption"])
    blip_model = BlipForConditionalGeneration.from_pretrained(
        MODEL_NAMES["caption"]
    ).to(device)

    clip_processor = CLIPProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAMES["clip"])
    clip_model = CLIPModel.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAMES["clip"]).to(device)

    _models.update({
        "device": device,
        "blip_processor": blip_processor,
        "blip_model": blip_model,
        "clip_processor": clip_processor,
        "clip_model": clip_model,
    })
    return _models


def _caption_image(pil_image) -> str:
    import torch
    m = _get_models()
    inputs = m["blip_processor"](pil_image, return_tensors="pt").to(m["device"])
    with torch.no_grad():
        out = m["blip_model"].generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=40)
    return m["blip_processor"].decode(out[0], skip_special_tokens=True)


def _clip_scores(pil_image, labels: List[str]) -> List[float]:
    """Return CLIP cosine-similarity-based probabilities for each label,
    normalized via softmax over this specific label set (a fresh
    zero-shot classification per attribute group).
    """
    import torch
    m = _get_models()
    inputs = m["clip_processor"](
        text=labels, images=pil_image, return_tensors="pt", padding=True
    ).to(m["device"])
    with torch.no_grad():
        outputs = m["clip_model"](**inputs)
        probs = outputs.logits_per_image.softmax(dim=1)[0]
    return probs.tolist()


def _call_vision_model(pil_image) -> dict:
    """Runs BLIP captioning + CLIP zero-shot attribute classification and
    returns the normalized dict shape expected by `extract_visual_features`.
    """
    caption = _caption_image(pil_image)

    room_scores = _clip_scores(pil_image, ROOM_TYPE_LABELS)
    condition_scores = _clip_scores(pil_image, CONDITION_LABELS)
    style_scores = _clip_scores(pil_image, STYLE_LABELS)
    amenity_scores = _clip_scores(pil_image, AMENITY_LABELS)

    room_idx = int(np.argmax(room_scores))
    condition_idx = int(np.argmax(condition_scores))

    style_tags = [
        label for label, score in zip(STYLE_LABELS, style_scores)
        if score >= _TAG_THRESHOLD
    ]
    detected_amenities = [
        label for label, score in zip(AMENITY_LABELS, amenity_scores)
        if score >= _TAG_THRESHOLD
    ]

    # Overall confidence: how peaked the room-type distribution is â€”
    # a reasonable single scalar signal for how "sure" this pass was.
    confidence = float(room_scores[room_idx])

    return {
        "room_type": ROOM_TYPE_LABELS[room_idx],
        "condition": CONDITION_LABELS[condition_idx],
        "style_tags": style_tags,
        "detected_amenities": detected_amenities,
        "caption": caption,
        "confidence": confidence,
        "_scores": {
            "room_type": dict(zip(ROOM_TYPE_LABELS, room_scores)),
            "condition": dict(zip(CONDITION_LABELS, condition_scores)),
        },
    }


def extract_visual_features(
    source: Union[str, Path, bytes, np.ndarray],
    source_file: Optional[str] = None,
    preprocess_config: Optional[ImagePreprocessConfig] = None,
) -> VisualFeatures:
    """Run preprocessing + the vision model on a single property image and
    return normalized VisualFeatures for downstream normalization/indexing.
    """
    # Property photos should generally keep color + not be deskewed
    # aggressively â€” override defaults sensibly for this use case.
    config = preprocess_config or ImagePreprocessConfig(
        deskew=False, to_grayscale=False,
    )
    img = preprocess_image(source, config)
    pil_img = to_pil(img)

    result = _call_vision_model(pil_img)

    return VisualFeatures(
        source_file=source_file or (str(source) if isinstance(source, (str, Path)) else "in_memory"),
        room_type=result.get("room_type"),
        condition=result.get("condition"),
        style_tags=result.get("style_tags", []),
        detected_amenities=result.get("detected_amenities", []),
        caption=result.get("caption"),
        confidence=float(result.get("confidence", 0.0)),
        raw_model_output=result,
    )


def extract_visual_features_batch(
    sources: List[Union[str, Path, bytes, np.ndarray]],
) -> List[VisualFeatures]:
    """Convenience batch wrapper. Swap for true batched inference later
    if your vision backend supports it â€” kept simple/sequential for now
    to match the MVP's "deterministic, traceable" design principle.
    """
    return [extract_visual_features(s) for s in sources]

from typing import List
import logging

from langchain_text_splitters import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


# Chunking configuration
CHUNK_SIZE = 1500
CHUNK_OVERLAP = 100


def chunk_text(
    text: str,
    chunk_size: int = CHUNK_SIZE,
    chunk_overlap: int = CHUNK_OVERLAP,
) -> List[str]:
    """
    Split text into meaningful chunks using recursive character splitting.

    The splitter tries to preserve structure by splitting on:
    paragraphs -> lines -> sentences -> words -> characters.

    Args:
        text: Input text.
        chunk_size: Maximum size of each chunk in characters.
        chunk_overlap: Number of overlapping characters between chunks.

    Returns:
        A list of non-empty text chunks.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If chunk_size or chunk_overlap is invalid.
    """

    # Validate input
    if not text or not text.strip():
        logger.warning("Chunking skipped: empty text received")
        return []

    if chunk_size <= 0:
        raise ValueError("chunk_size must be greater than 0")

    if chunk_overlap < 0:
        raise ValueError("chunk_overlap cannot be negative")

    if chunk_overlap >= chunk_size:
        raise ValueError(
            "chunk_overlap must be smaller than chunk_size"
        )

    text = text.strip()

    logger.info(
        "Starting text chunking | text_length=%d | chunk_size=%d | chunk_overlap=%d",
        len(text),
        chunk_size,
        chunk_overlap,
    )

    try:
        # Create recursive splitter
        splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
            chunk_size=chunk_size,
            chunk_overlap=chunk_overlap,
            separators=[
                "\n\n",  # Paragraphs
                "\n",    # Lines
                ". ",    # Sentences
                " ",     # Words
                "",      # Characters
            ],
            length_function=len,
            is_separator_regex=False,
        )

        # Split text
        chunks = splitter.split_text(text)

        # Remove empty chunks
        valid_chunks = [
            chunk.strip()
            for chunk in chunks
            if chunk.strip()
        ]

        logger.info(
            "Text chunking completed | chunks=%d | text_length=%d",
            len(valid_chunks),
            len(text),
        )

        return valid_chunks

    except Exception:
        logger.exception(
            "Text chunking failed | text_length=%d",
            len(text),
        )
        raise

from pathlib import Path
import logging

from PIL import Image

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS = {
    ".jpg",
    ".jpeg",
    ".png",
    ".webp",
    ".bmp",
    ".tiff",
    ".tif",
}


def load_image(file_path: str) -> Image.Image:
    """
    Load and validate an image file.

    Supported formats:
        - JPG / JPEG
        - PNG
        - WEBP
        - BMP
        - TIFF

    Args:
        file_path: Path to the image file.

    Returns:
        PIL Image object.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: If the image does not exist.
        ValueError: If the image format is unsupported.
        Exception: If the image cannot be opened.
    """

    logger.info("Starting image loading: %s", file_path)

    try:
        path = Path(file_path)

        # Validate file exists
        if not path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"Image file not found: {file_path}"
            )

        # Validate extension
        extension = path.suffix.lower()

        if extension not in SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported image format: {extension}. "
                f"Supported formats: {SUPPORTED_EXTENSIONS}"
            )

        # Open image
        image = Image.open(path)

        # Force loading to detect corrupted files early
        image.load()

        logger.info(
            "Image loaded successfully | file=%s | format=%s | size=%s | mode=%s",
            file_path,
            image.format,
            image.size,
            image.mode,
        )

        return image

    except Exception:
        logger.exception(
            "Image loading failed | file=%s",
            file_path,
        )
        raise

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def build_metadata(
    file_path: str,
    *,
    source_type: str | None = None,
    property_id: str | None = None,
    extra_metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Build standardized metadata for an ingested document.

    Metadata is attached to documents/chunks and can later be used for:
    - filtering
    - retrieval
    - tracing
    - source attribution
    - property-level grouping
    """

    path = Path(file_path)

    metadata: dict[str, Any] = {
        "source": path.name,
        "source_path": str(path),
        "file_name": path.name,
        "file_extension": path.suffix.lower(),
    }

    if source_type:
        metadata["source_type"] = source_type

    if property_id:
        metadata["property_id"] = property_id

    if extra_metadata:
        metadata.update(extra_metadata)

    logger.debug(
        "Metadata created | file=%s | property_id=%s | keys=%s",
        file_path,
        property_id,
        list(metadata.keys()),
    )

    return metadata


def add_chunk_metadata(
    metadata: dict[str, Any],
    *,
    chunk_index: int,
    total_chunks: int | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Add chunk-level metadata to an existing metadata dictionary.
    """

    chunk_metadata = metadata.copy()

    chunk_metadata["chunk_index"] = chunk_index

    if total_chunks is not None:
        chunk_metadata["total_chunks"] = total_chunks

    return chunk_metadata

import logging
from pathlib import Path


logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def parse_office(file_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Parse Office documents such as DOCX and PPTX using Unstructured.

    Unstructured automatically detects the document type
    and extracts its textual content.
    """

    logger.info("Starting Office document parsing: %s", file_path)

    try:
        path = Path(file_path)
        if not path.exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"Office file not found: {file_path}"
            )

        if path.suffix.lower() not in {".docx", ".pptx"}:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unsupported Office format: {path.suffix}"
            )

        # Imported lazily: importing unstructured is slow (and can block on
        # first-run downloads), which must not delay API startup.
        from unstructured.partition.auto import partition

        elements = partition(filename=str(path))

        full_text = "\n".join(
            str(element).strip()
            for element in elements
            if str(element).strip()
        )

        if not full_text:
            logger.warning(
                "Unstructured returned empty text: %s",
                file_path,
            )
        else:
            logger.info(
                "Office document parsed successfully: %s | "
                "characters=%d | elements=%d",
                file_path,
                len(full_text),
                len(elements),
            )

        return full_text

    except Exception:
        logger.exception(
            "Office document parsing failed: %s",
            file_path,
        )
        raise

from pathlib import Path
import logging
import os
import tempfile

from pypdf import PdfReader

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


def parse_pdf(file_path: str) -> str:
    """
    Extract text from a PDF locally using pypdf.

    Falls back to pdfplumber for pages where pypdf
    fails to extract meaningful text.
    """

    logger.info("Starting PDF parsing: %s", file_path)

    try:
        reader = PdfReader(file_path)
        total_pages = len(reader.pages)

        logger.info(
            "PDF loaded | filename=%s | total_pages=%d",
            file_path,
            total_pages,
        )

        page_texts: list[str | None] = [None] * total_pages
        blank_pages: list[int] = []

        # Primary extraction using pypdf
        for i, page in enumerate(reader.pages):
            text = page.extract_text() or ""

            if text.strip():
                page_texts[i] = text
            else:
                blank_pages.append(i + 1)

        # Fallback extraction using pdfplumber
        if blank_pages:
            logger.info(
                "Some pages returned no text from pypdf | blank_pages=%s",
                blank_pages,
            )

            try:
                import pdfplumber

                with pdfplumber.open(file_path) as pdf:
                    for page_num in blank_pages:
                        page = pdf.pages[page_num - 1]
                        fallback_text = page.extract_text() or ""

                        if fallback_text.strip():
                            page_texts[page_num - 1] = fallback_text

            except Exception:
                logger.exception(
                    "pdfplumber fallback failed | filename=%s",
                    file_path,
                )

        # Preserve original page order
        full_text = "\n\n".join(
            text.strip()
            for text in page_texts
            if text and text.strip()
        )

        if not full_text:
            logger.warning(
                "No text extracted; applying OCR to PDF pages | filename=%s",
                file_path,
            )
            try:
                import fitz

                from app.rag.ocr.extractor import OCRExtractor
                from app.rag.ocr.post_processor import OCRPostProcessor

                extractor = OCRExtractor()
                ocr_pages: list[str] = []
                with fitz.open(file_path) as document:
                    for page in document:
                        temporary_path: str | None = None
                        try:
                            with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, suffix=".png") as temporary:
                                temporary_path = temporary.name
                            page.get_pixmap(matrix=fitz.Matrix(2, 2)).save(temporary_path)
                            text = extractor.extract_from_image(temporary_path)
                            if text.strip():
                                ocr_pages.append(text)
                        finally:
                            if temporary_path and os.path.exists(temporary_path):
                                os.unlink(temporary_path)
                full_text = OCRPostProcessor().process("\n\n".join(ocr_pages)).text
            except Exception:
                logger.exception("PDF OCR fallback failed | filename=%s", file_path)
        else:
            logger.info(
                "PDF text extracted successfully | filename=%s | characters=%d",
                file_path,
                len(full_text),
            )

        return full_text

    except Exception:
        logger.exception(
            "PDF parsing failed | filename=%s",
            file_path,
        )
        raise
