"""Gemini Live resilience: reconnects, interruptions and tool-call cancellation.

The Live provider is faked (see conftest); the voice bridge, the agent graph and
the database are the real code.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import threading
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from starlette.websockets import WebSocketDisconnect

from tests.conftest import (
    live_audio,
    live_event,
    live_go_away,
    live_tool_call,
    live_tool_cancellation,
)
from tests.integration.test_api_channels import chat, client, receive_until, voice_token  # noqa: F401

ORIGIN = {"origin": "http://testserver"}


def connect(client, token):
    return client.websocket_connect(f"/website/voice?token={token}", headers=ORIGIN)


def test_provider_go_away_reconnects_without_dropping_the_browser_socket(client, fake_live, stub_rag, settings_env):
    settings_env(VOICE_RECONNECT_BACKOFF_SECONDS="0")
    session_id = chat(client, "villa in Sheikh Zayed")["session_id"]
    token = voice_token(client, session_id)["token"]
    fake_live.install_sequence(
        [[live_audio(b"A\x00"), live_go_away()]],
        [[live_audio(b"B\x00"), live_event(turn_complete=True)]],
    )

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        assert json.loads(ws.receive()["text"])["type"] == "ready"
        ws.send_bytes(b"\x00\x00" * 10)
        first = receive_until(ws, "reconnected")
        assert ("audio", b"A\x00") in first
        assert ("event", {"type": "reconnecting"}) in first

        ws.send_bytes(b"\x00\x00" * 10)  # same browser socket, new provider session
        second = receive_until(ws, "turn_complete")
        assert ("audio", b"B\x00") in second

    assert fake_live.connections == 2
    # The second session was briefed again from the stored conversation.
    assert all("Sheikh Zayed" in instruction for instruction in fake_live.instructions)


def test_audio_captured_during_the_reconnect_gap_is_not_lost(client, fake_live, settings_env):
    settings_env(VOICE_RECONNECT_BACKOFF_SECONDS="0")
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]
    fake_live.install_sequence([[live_go_away()]], [[live_event(turn_complete=True)]])

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        ws.receive()
        for index in range(1, 4):  # frames 2 and 3 arrive while reconnecting
            ws.send_bytes(bytes([index, 0]) * 8)
        receive_until(ws, "turn_complete")

    delivered = [frame for session in fake_live.sessions for frame in session.audio]
    assert delivered[0] == bytes([1, 0]) * 8
    assert bytes([2, 0]) * 8 in delivered or bytes([3, 0]) * 8 in delivered


def test_cancelled_tool_call_is_not_answered(client, fake_live, stub_rag):
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]
    session = fake_live.install([
        [live_tool_call("villa in Sheikh Zayed", call_id="call-9"), live_tool_cancellation("call-9")],
        [live_event(turn_complete=True)],
    ])

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        ws.receive()
        ws.send_bytes(b"\x00\x00" * 10)
        receive_until(ws, "agent_result")  # the work still ran...
        ws.send_bytes(b"\x00\x00" * 10)
        receive_until(ws, "turn_complete")

    assert session.tool_responses == []  # ...but the model no longer wanted the answer


def test_interruption_is_delivered_while_the_agent_is_still_working(client, fake_live, monkeypatch):
    """The old inline tool handling would have held the interruption back until
    the (up to 30 s) agent turn finished."""
    import app.channels.website as website

    release = threading.Event()

    def slow_turn(thread_id, message, **_):
        release.wait(timeout=10)
        return SimpleNamespace(response="done", intent="x", to_dict=lambda: {"response": "done", "intent": "x"})

    monkeypatch.setattr(website, "conversation_service", SimpleNamespace(run_turn=slow_turn, context_summary=lambda _t: ""))
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]
    fake_live.install([[live_tool_call("anything"), live_event(interrupted=True)], [live_event(turn_complete=True)]])

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        ws.receive()
        ws.send_bytes(b"\x00\x00" * 10)
        seen = receive_until(ws, "interrupted")  # arrives although the agent has not finished
        assert not any(kind == "event" and payload["type"] == "agent_result" for kind, payload in seen)
        release.set()
        receive_until(ws, "agent_result")


def test_idle_call_ends_with_a_reason(client, fake_live, settings_env):
    settings_env(VOICE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS="0")
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]
    fake_live.install([])
    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        ws.receive()
        frames = receive_until(ws, "session_end")
    assert frames[-1] == ("event", {"type": "session_end", "reason": "idle"})


def test_voice_connections_are_rate_limited_and_capped_per_client(client, fake_live, settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_VOICE_CONNECT_PER_MINUTE="2", VOICE_MAX_SESSIONS_PER_IP="1")
    fake_live.install([])
    tokens = [voice_token(client)["token"] for _ in range(3)]

    with connect(client, tokens[0]) as first:
        assert json.loads(first.receive()["text"])["type"] == "ready"
        # Second concurrent call from the same address: refused as busy.
        with connect(client, tokens[1]) as second:
            assert json.loads(second.receive()["text"])["code"] == "busy"

    # The handshake budget (2 per minute) is spent, so a third attempt is refused outright.
    with pytest.raises(WebSocketDisconnect):
        with connect(client, tokens[2]) as third:
            third.receive()


def _provider_fails(monkeypatch, error):
    """Every attempt to open a Gemini Live session raises ``error``; returns the attempt list."""
    from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

    import app.channels.website as website

    attempts = []

    @asynccontextmanager
    async def connect(system_instruction=None, **_):
        attempts.append(1)
        raise error
        yield  # pragma: no cover - makes this an async generator

    monkeypatch.setattr(website, "connect_live_session", connect)
    return attempts


def test_gemini_quota_error_is_reported_as_busy_and_not_retried(client, monkeypatch, settings_env):
    """A 429 from Gemini used to look like 'the connection dropped' and was retried, burning more quota."""
    settings_env(VOICE_RECONNECT_BACKOFF_SECONDS="0")
    attempts = _provider_fails(monkeypatch, RuntimeError("429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: quota exceeded for this model"))
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        event = json.loads(ws.receive()["text"])

    assert event["type"] == "error" and event["code"] == "busy"
    assert len(attempts) == 1
    assert "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED" not in json.dumps(event)  # provider detail stays in the server log


def test_other_provider_failures_are_still_retried_then_reported_as_disconnected(client, monkeypatch, settings_env):
    settings_env(VOICE_RECONNECT_BACKOFF_SECONDS="0", VOICE_MAX_PROVIDER_RECONNECTS="2")
    attempts = _provider_fails(monkeypatch, ConnectionError("network unreachable"))
    token = voice_token(client)["token"]

    with connect(client, token) as ws:
        frames = receive_until(ws, "error")

    assert frames[-1][1]["code"] == "provider_disconnected"
    assert len(attempts) == 3  # first try + 2 reconnects


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "error, expected",
    [
        (RuntimeError("429 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"), True),
        (RuntimeError("Resource has been exhausted (e.g. check quota)."), True),
        (type("QuotaError", (Exception,), {"code": 429})(), True),
        (ConnectionError("connection reset"), False),
        (ValueError("model not found"), False),
    ],
)
def test_quota_errors_are_recognised(error, expected):
    from app.channels.website import is_provider_quota_error

    assert is_provider_quota_error(error) is expected

"""Meta WhatsApp Cloud API webhook: signatures, duplicates, retries, floods, odd payloads.

Meta itself is simulated (signed payloads in Meta's documented shape); the
FastAPI app, the agent graph and PostgreSQL/SQLite storage are the real code.
These tests prove our side of the contract, not that Meta accepts our token.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import json

import pytest

import app.api.routes.webhooks as webhooks
from app.database import models as db
from app.database.session import session_scope
from tests.integration.test_api_channels import client  # noqa: F401  (fixture)

SECRET = "app-secret"
PHONE_ID = "1234567890"


@pytest.fixture
def wa(client, stub_rag, settings_env, monkeypatch):
    settings_env(WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET=SECRET, WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN="verify-me", WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID=PHONE_ID,
                 WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN="token")
    sent: list[tuple[str, str]] = []

    async def fake_send(recipient, text):
        sent.append((recipient, text))

    monkeypatch.setattr(webhooks, "send_text_message", fake_send)

    class Meta:
        def payload(self, *messages, phone_number_id=PHONE_ID, extra=None):
            value = {"messaging_product": "whatsapp", "metadata": {"phone_number_id": phone_number_id}, "messages": list(messages)}
            value.update(extra or {})
            return json.dumps({"object": "whatsapp_business_account", "entry": [{"id": "1", "changes": [{"field": "messages", "value": value}]}]}).encode()

        def post(self, body, secret=SECRET, signature=None):
            sig = signature or "sha256=" + hmac.new(secret.encode(), body, hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
            return client.post("/whatsapp/webhook", content=body, headers={"X-Hub-Signature-256": sig, "Content-Type": "application/json"})

        def text(self, message_id, body, sender="201000000001"):
            return {"id": message_id, "from": sender, "timestamp": "1760000000", "type": "text", "text": {"body": body}}

    meta = Meta()
    meta.sent = sent
    meta.client = client
    return meta


def claims():
    with session_scope() as session:
        return {(row.kind, row.key): row.status for row in session.query(db.ReplayGuard)}

def test_verification_handshake_echoes_the_challenge_only_for_the_right_token(wa):
    ok = wa.client.get("/whatsapp/webhook", params={"hub.mode": "subscribe", "hub.verify_token": "verify-me", "hub.challenge": "98765"})
    assert (ok.status_code, ok.text) == (200, "98765")
    assert ok.headers["content-type"].startswith("text/plain")
    for params in (
        {"hub.mode": "subscribe", "hub.verify_token": "wrong", "hub.challenge": "1"},
        {"hub.mode": "unsubscribe", "hub.verify_token": "verify-me", "hub.challenge": "1"},
        {"hub.mode": "subscribe", "hub.verify_token": "verify-me"},
        {},
    ):
        assert wa.client.get("/whatsapp/webhook", params=params).status_code == 403

def test_a_failed_message_is_retried_on_redelivery_and_the_customer_is_told_meanwhile(wa, monkeypatch):
    real = webhooks.run_whatsapp_turn
    calls = {"n": 0}

    def flaky(*args, **kwargs):
        calls["n"] += 1
        if calls["n"] == 1:
            raise TimeoutError("provider timed out")
        return real(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(webhooks, "run_whatsapp_turn", flaky)
    body = wa.payload(wa.text("wamid.retry", "villa in Sheikh Zayed"))

    wa.post(body)
    assert claims()[("whatsapp", "wamid.retry")] == "failed"
    assert len(wa.sent) == 1 and "try again" in wa.sent[0][1].lower()  # the customer is not left in silence

    wa.post(body)  # Meta redelivers
    assert claims()[("whatsapp", "wamid.retry")] == "done"
    assert len(wa.sent) == 2 and "501189949" in wa.sent[1][1]  # now they get the real answer


def test_a_message_abandoned_by_a_crashed_worker_can_be_picked_up_again(wa):
    from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

    from app.database import replay

    assert replay.claim("whatsapp", "wamid.crash", ttl_seconds=600)  # a worker claimed it, then died
    body = wa.payload(wa.text("wamid.crash", "villa in Sheikh Zayed"))
    wa.post(body)

        session.query(db.ReplayGuard).update({"created_at": datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(minutes=10)})
    wa.post(body)
    assert len(wa.sent) == 1

def test_gateway_failure_leaves_the_message_retryable(wa, settings_env, monkeypatch):
    settings_env(WHATSAPP_GATEWAY_SECRET="gw-secret")
    real = webhooks.run_whatsapp_turn
    state = {"fail": True}

    def flaky(*args, **kwargs):
        if state["fail"]:
            raise TimeoutError("boom")
        return real(*args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(webhooks, "run_whatsapp_turn", flaky)
    body = {"message_id": "gw-1", "sender": "201000000002@c.us", "text": "hello"}

    failed = wa.client.post("/internal/whatsapp/message", json=body, headers=headers)
    assert failed.status_code == 500 and failed.json() == {"detail": "Internal server error"}
    assert claims()[("whatsapp_gateway", "gw-1")] == "failed"
    state["fail"] = False  # the gateway retries; the message is not stuck as a "duplicate"
    assert wa.client.post("/internal/whatsapp/message", json=body, headers=headers).json()["reply"]

def need(*names: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    missing = [name for name in names if not LIVE_ENV.get(name)]
    if missing:
        pytest.skip("not verified - missing credential(s): " + ", ".join(missing))
    return {name: LIVE_ENV[name] for name in names}


def cosine(a: list[float], b: list[float]) -> float:
    return sum(x * y for x, y in zip(a, b)) / (math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in a)) * math.sqrt(sum(y * y for y in b)))


@pytest.fixture
def live_settings(settings_env):
    """Apply the real credentials this process captured at start-up."""
    keep = ("GEMINI_API_KEY", "GROQ_API_KEY", "QDRANT_URL", "QDRANT_API_KEY", "GEMINI_LIVE_MODEL", "GEMINI_VOICE",
            "EMBEDDING_DIMENSION", "EMBEDDING_MODEL", "GROQ_MODEL", "WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN", "WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID")
    settings_env(**{key: LIVE_ENV[key] for key in keep if LIVE_ENV.get(key)})
    return LIVE_ENV

def test_index_search_roundtrip_with_filters_in_two_languages(scratch_collection):

def test_gemini_live_accepts_our_config_and_calls_the_agent_tool(live_settings):
    need("GEMINI_API_KEY")
    from app.voice.gemini_live import AGENT_TOOL_NAME, build_voice_instruction, connect_live_session

    async def run() -> tuple[bool, list[str]]:
        tool_called, transcripts = False, []
        async with connect_live_session(build_voice_instruction("ar")) as session:
            await session.send_realtime_input(text="I am looking for an apartment in New Cairo. What do you have?")
            async with asyncio.timeout(40):
                async for message in session.receive():
                    call = getattr(message, "tool_call", None)
                    if call is not None:
                        names = [item.name for item in call.function_calls or []]
                        tool_called = AGENT_TOOL_NAME in names
                        return tool_called, transcripts
                    content = getattr(message, "server_content", None)
                    text = getattr(getattr(content, "output_transcription", None), "text", None)
                    if text:
                        transcripts.append(text)
                    if content is not None and getattr(content, "turn_complete", False):
                        break
        return tool_called, transcripts

    called, transcripts = asyncio.run(run())
    assert called, f"model answered from its own knowledge instead of calling the tool: {''.join(transcripts)[:200]}"

        f"https://graph.facebook.com/{LIVE_ENV.get('WHATSAPP_API_VERSION', 'v23.0')}/{LIVE_ENV['WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID']}",
        params={"fields": "display_phone_number,verified_name"},
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {LIVE_ENV['WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN']}"},
        timeout=20,
    )
    assert response.status_code == 200, f"Meta rejected the credentials (HTTP {response.status_code})"
    assert response.json().get("display_phone_number")


def _live_exchange(language: str, customer_text: str, reply: str | None = None) -> tuple[str | None, str]:
    """Send one text turn to the real Live model.

    Returns (the ``message`` it put in the tool call, what it said after receiving
    ``reply`` as the tool result).
    """
    from google.genai import types

    from app.voice.gemini_live import AGENT_TOOL_NAME, build_voice_instruction, connect_live_session

    async def run() -> tuple[str | None, str]:
        tool_message, spoken = None, []
        async with connect_live_session(build_voice_instruction(language)) as session:
            await session.send_realtime_input(text=customer_text)
            async with asyncio.timeout(60):
                while True:
                    async for message in session.receive():
                        call = getattr(message, "tool_call", None)
                        if call is not None:
                            for item in call.function_calls or []:
                                if item.name == AGENT_TOOL_NAME:
                                    tool_message = str((item.args or {}).get("message", ""))
                                    if reply is None:
                                        return tool_message, ""
                                    await session.send_tool_response(function_responses=[
                                        types.FunctionResponse(id=item.id, name=item.name, response={"reply": reply})
                                    ])
                        content = getattr(message, "server_content", None)
                        text = getattr(getattr(content, "output_transcription", None), "text", None)
                        if text:
                            spoken.append(text)
                        if content is not None and getattr(content, "turn_complete", False) and (tool_message is None or spoken):
                            return tool_message, "".join(spoken)

    return asyncio.run(run())


def test_gemini_live_arabic_conversation_stays_in_arabic(live_settings):
    need("GEMINI_API_KEY")
    import re

    tool_message, spoken = _live_exchange(
        "ar", "Ø¹Ø§ÙŠØ² Ø´Ù‚Ø© ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„ØªØ¬Ù…Ø¹ Ø§Ù„Ø®Ø§Ù…Ø³ Ù…ÙŠØ²Ø§Ù†ÙŠØªÙŠ Ø®Ù…Ø³Ø© Ù…Ù„ÙŠÙˆÙ†",
        reply="Ù„Ù‚ÙŠØª Ù„Ùƒ Ø´Ù‚Ø© ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„ØªØ¬Ù…Ø¹ Ø§Ù„Ø®Ø§Ù…Ø³ØŒ ØªÙ„Ø§Øª ØºØ±Ù Ù†ÙˆÙ…ØŒ Ø³Ø¹Ø±Ù‡Ø§ 5,200,000 Ø¬Ù†ÙŠÙ‡.",
    )
    assert tool_message and re.search(r"[Ø€-Û¿]", tool_message), f"tool message was not forwarded in Arabic: {tool_message!r}"
    assert re.search(r"[Ø€-Û¿]", spoken), f"the spoken reply was not Arabic: {spoken!r}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("utterance", [
    "Ø±Ù‚Ù… ØªÙ„ÙŠÙÙˆÙ†ÙŠ ØµÙØ± ÙˆØ§Ø­Ø¯ ØµÙØ± ÙˆØ§Ø­Ø¯ Ø§ØªÙ†ÙŠÙ† ØªÙ„Ø§ØªØ© Ø§Ø±Ø¨Ø¹Ø© Ø®Ù…Ø³Ø© Ø³ØªØ© Ø³Ø¨Ø¹Ø© ØªÙ…Ø§Ù†ÙŠØ©",
    "my phone number is zero one zero, one two three, four five six seven eight",
])
def test_phone_number_dictated_to_the_live_model_reaches_the_agent_intact(live_settings, utterance):
    """Digits spoken in words must come out of the model and through our parser as one valid number."""
    need("GEMINI_API_KEY")
    from app.agents.understanding import extract_qualification
    from app.helpers.phone import normalize_phone

    tool_message, _ = _live_exchange("ar" if utterance[0] == "Ø±" else "en", utterance)

    captured = extract_qualification(tool_message).get("phone")
    assert normalize_phone(captured) == "+201012345678", f"captured {captured!r} from tool message {tool_message!r}"

# Needs the offline ingestion extras (requirements-ingest.txt); skipped on the lean API install.
import pytest as _pytest
_pytest.importorskip("cv2")
_pytest.importorskip("numpy")

import pytest
import numpy as np
import cv2
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
from app.rag.cv.floorplan_parser import parse_floorplan, FloorplanResult

def create_synthetic_floorplan(num_rooms=3):
    """
    Creates a white image with black rectangles representing rooms.
    """
    img = np.full((500, 500, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
    # Room sizes and positions
    rooms = [
        (50, 50, 80, 80),
        (200, 50, 80, 120),
        (300, 200, 80, 80),
    ][:num_rooms]

    for (x, y, w, h) in rooms:
        cv2.rectangle(img, (x, y), (x + w, y + h), (0, 0, 0), -1)

    return img

def test_parse_floorplan_basic():
    img = create_synthetic_floorplan(num_rooms=3)
    # We use bytes to test the load_image integration within parse_floorplan
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img)
    img_bytes = buffer.tobytes()

    result = parse_floorplan(img_bytes)

    assert isinstance(result, FloorplanResult)
    assert result.room_count_estimate == 3
    assert len(result.regions) == 3
    assert result.confidence > 0

def test_parse_floorplan_empty():
    # Pure white image
    img = np.full((500, 500, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img)
    img_bytes = buffer.tobytes()

    result = parse_floorplan(img_bytes)

    assert result.room_count_estimate == 0
    assert "No room regions detected" in result.notes[0]
    assert result.confidence == 0.0

def test_parse_floorplan_large_noise():
    # Image with one giant rectangle (too large to be a room)
    img = np.full((500, 500, 3), 255, dtype=np.uint8)
    cv2.rectangle(img, (10, 10), (490, 490), (0, 0, 0), -1)
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode(".jpg", img)
    img_bytes = buffer.tobytes()

    result = parse_floorplan(img_bytes)

    # Should filter out the outer contour
    assert result.room_count_estimate == 0

import pytest as _pytest

import pytest

from PIL import Image
from app.rag.cv.image_processor import (
    load_image,
    preprocess_image,
    to_pil,
    ImagePreprocessConfig,
)

@pytest.fixture
def sample_image_array():
    """Create a simple 100x100 BGR image."""
    return np.full((100, 100, 3), (255, 0, 0), dtype=np.uint8)

@pytest.fixture
def sample_image_path(tmp_path, sample_image_array):
    """Save a sample image to a temporary file."""
    path = tmp_path / "test_image.jpg"
    cv2.imwrite(str(path), sample_image_array)
    return str(path)

def test_load_image_array(sample_image_array):
    img = load_image(sample_image_array)
    assert np.array_equal(img, sample_image_array)

def test_load_image_path(sample_image_path):
    img = load_image(sample_image_path)
    assert img is not None
    assert img.shape == (100, 100, 3)

def test_load_image_bytes(sample_image_array):
    _, buffer = cv2.imencode(".jpg", sample_image_array)
    bytes_data = buffer.tobytes()
    img = load_image(bytes_data)
    assert img is not None
    # Note: JPEG compression might change pixels slightly, but shape should match
    assert img.shape == (100, 100, 3)

def test_load_image_invalid_path():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Could not read image at path"):
        load_image("non_existent_file.jpg")

def test_preprocess_image_grayscale(sample_image_array):
    config = ImagePreprocessConfig(to_grayscale=True, deskew=False, denoise=False)
    img = preprocess_image(sample_image_array, config)
    assert img.ndim == 2  # Grayscale should be 2D

def test_preprocess_image_resize(sample_image_array):
    # Create a larger image
    large_img = np.full((3000, 1000, 3), (255, 0, 0), dtype=np.uint8)
    config = ImagePreprocessConfig(max_dimension=1000, deskew=False, denoise=False)
    img = preprocess_image(large_img, config)
    assert max(img.shape[:2]) <= 1000

def test_to_pil_rgb(sample_image_array):
    pil_img = to_pil(sample_image_array)
    assert isinstance(pil_img, Image.Image)
    assert pil_img.mode == "RGB"

def test_to_pil_grayscale():
    gray_img = np.full((100, 100), 128, dtype=np.uint8)
    pil_img = to_pil(gray_img)
    assert isinstance(pil_img, Image.Image)
    assert pil_img.mode == "L"

def test_extract_visual_features_logic(mock_image):
    """
    Test the orchestration logic of extract_visual_features by mocking

    """
    mock_result = {
        "room_type": "living room",
        "condition": "good condition",
        "style_tags": ["modern", "furnished"],

        "caption": "A modern living room with a balcony",

        },
    }

    # We patch _call_vision_model to avoid loading real weights
    with patch("app.rag.cv.vision_extractor._call_vision_model", return_value=mock_result):
        features = extract_visual_features(mock_image, source_file="test.jpg")

        assert isinstance(features, VisualFeatures)
        assert features.source_file == "test.jpg"

        assert features.condition == "good condition"
        assert "modern" in features.style_tags
        assert "balcony" in features.detected_amenities
        assert features.caption == "A modern living room with a balcony"
        assert features.confidence == 0.85
        assert features.raw_model_output == mock_result

        answer, cited = generation._extract_cited_ids(raw)

        assert answer == "Ù„Ù‚ÙŠØª A102."
        assert cited == ["A102", "B205"]

    def test_invalid_citation_value_types_are_ignored(self):
        raw = (
            'Ø±Ø¯.\n'
            '{"cited_property_ids": ["A102", null, {}, 123]}'
        )

        answer, cited = generation._extract_cited_ids(raw)

        assert answer == "Ø±Ø¯."
        assert cited == ["A102", "123"]

class TestGenerateResponse:

    def test_generate_response_happy_path(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        fake_completion = make_fake_completion(
            'Ù„Ù‚ÙŠØª Ù„Ùƒ Ø´Ù‚ØªÙŠÙ† ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„ØªØ¬Ù…Ø¹: A102 Ùˆ B205.\n'
            '{"cited_property_ids": ["A102", "B205"]}'
        )

        fake_client = MagicMock()
        fake_client.chat.completions.create.return_value = fake_completion

        with patch.object(
            generation,
            "_get_client",
            return_value=fake_client,
        ):
            result = generation.generate_response(
                "Ø¹Ø§ÙŠØ² Ø´Ù‚Ø© 3 ØºØ±Ù ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„ØªØ¬Ù…Ø¹",
                candidates,
            )

        expected_model = generation._get_model_name()

        assert isinstance(
            result,
            generation.GenerationResult,
        )
        assert "A102" in result.answer_text
        assert result.cited_property_ids == [
            "A102",
            "B205",
        ]
        assert result.grounding_property_ids == [
            "A102",
            "B205",
        ]
        assert result.model == expected_model
        assert result.raw_response == {
            "id": "fake-completion"
        }

        _, kwargs = (
            fake_client
            .chat
            .completions
            .create.call_args
        )

        assert kwargs["model"] == expected_model
        assert kwargs["messages"][-1]["content"] == (
            "Ø¹Ø§ÙŠØ² Ø´Ù‚Ø© 3 ØºØ±Ù ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„ØªØ¬Ù…Ø¹"
        )

    def test_generate_response_no_candidates(self):
        """No evidence means no model call: the reply is fixed text, never invented."""
        fake_client = MagicMock()

        with patch.object(generation, "_get_client", return_value=fake_client):
            arabic = generation.generate_response("Ø¹Ø§ÙŠØ² ÙÙŠÙ„Ø§ ÙÙŠ Ø§Ù„Ù…Ø±ÙŠØ® Ø¨Ù…Ù„ÙŠÙˆÙ† Ø¬Ù†ÙŠÙ‡", [])
            english = generation.generate_response("villa on Mars for one million", [])

        fake_client.chat.completions.create.assert_not_called()
        for result in (arabic, english):
            assert result.cited_property_ids == []
            assert result.grounding_property_ids == []
        assert "Ù…ÙÙŠØ´ Ø¹Ù‚Ø§Ø±Ø§Øª Ù…Ø·Ø§Ø¨Ù‚Ø©" in arabic.answer_text
        assert "couldn't find any listings" in english.answer_text
        # Fixed text promises nothing about prices, areas or availability.
        assert not any(character.isdigit() for character in english.answer_text)

    def test_generate_response_no_candidates_still_rejects_blank_query(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            generation.generate_response("   ", [])

    def test_generate_response_logs_hallucinated_citation(
        self,
        candidates,
        caplog,
    ):
        fake_completion = make_fake_completion(
            'ÙÙŠ Ø¹Ù‚Ø§Ø± ÙƒÙˆÙŠØ³ Ù„ÙŠÙƒ Ø§Ø³Ù…Ù‡ Z999.\n'
            '{"cited_property_ids": ["Z999"]}'
        )

        fake_client = MagicMock()
        fake_client.chat.completions.create.return_value = fake_completion

        with patch.object(
            generation,
            "_get_client",
            return_value=fake_client,
        ):
            with caplog.at_level(logging.WARNING):
                result = generation.generate_response(
                    "test query",
                    candidates,
                )

        assert result.cited_property_ids == []
        assert result.grounding_property_ids == [
            "A102",
            "B205",
        ]

        warnings = [
            record.getMessage()
            for record in caplog.records
            if record.levelno == logging.WARNING
        ]

        assert any(
            "absent from retrieved evidence" in message
            and "Z999" in message
            for message in warnings
        )

    def test_generate_response_passes_temperature_and_max_tokens(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        fake_completion = make_fake_completion(
            'Ø±Ø¯.\n{"cited_property_ids": []}'
        )

        fake_client = MagicMock()
        fake_client.chat.completions.create.return_value = fake_completion

        with patch.object(
            generation,
            "_get_client",
            return_value=fake_client,
        ):
            generation.generate_response(
                "test",
                candidates,
                temperature=0.5,
                max_tokens=200,
            )

        _, kwargs = (
            fake_client
            .chat
            .completions
            .create.call_args
        )

        assert kwargs["temperature"] == 0.5
        assert kwargs["max_tokens"] == 200

    def test_client_never_constructed_until_needed(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        """
        build_messages must not require GROQ_API_KEY or construct
        the Groq client.
        """
        generation.build_messages(
            "test",
            candidates,
        )

class TestGenerationParameterValidation:

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "temperature",
        [-0.1, 2.1, 3, -5],
    )
    def test_invalid_temperature_is_rejected(
        self,
        candidates,
        temperature,
    ):
        with pytest.raises(
            ValueError,
            match="temperature must be between 0 and 2",
        ):
            generation.generate_response(
                "test",
                candidates,
                temperature=temperature,
            )

    def test_non_numeric_temperature_is_rejected(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        with pytest.raises(
            TypeError,
            match="temperature must be a number",
        ):
            generation.generate_response(
                "test",
                candidates,
                temperature="low",
            )

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "max_tokens",
        [0, -1, -100],
    )
    def test_invalid_max_tokens_is_rejected(
        self,
        candidates,
        max_tokens,
    ):
        with pytest.raises(
            ValueError,
            match="max_tokens must be greater than 0",
        ):
            generation.generate_response(
                "test",
                candidates,
                max_tokens=max_tokens,
            )

    def test_non_integer_max_tokens_is_rejected(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        with pytest.raises(
            TypeError,
            match="max_tokens must be an integer",
        ):
            generation.generate_response(
                "test",
                candidates,
                max_tokens=100.5,
            )

class TestFinancialGuardrails:

    def test_removes_unsupported_down_payment_claim(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
Ù„Ù‚ÙŠØª Ù„Ùƒ ÙÙŠÙ„Ø§ Ù…Ù†Ø§Ø³Ø¨Ø©.

Down payment: 390,000 EGP

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "Down payment" not in cleaned
        assert "390,000" not in cleaned

    def test_payment_plan_does_not_authorize_down_payment(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
A102 Ù…ØªØ§Ø­ Ø¨Ù†Ø¸Ø§Ù… installment.

Down payment: 480,000 EGP

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "installment" in cleaned
        assert "Down payment" not in cleaned
        assert "480,000" not in cleaned

    def test_removes_unsupported_financial_table_column(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
| Property | Price | Down Payment |
|---|---:|---:|
| A102 | 4,800,000 | 480,000 |
| B205 | 4,950,000 | 495,000 |

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102", "B205"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "Down Payment" not in cleaned
        assert "480,000" not in cleaned
        assert "495,000" not in cleaned
        assert "4,800,000" in cleaned
        assert "4,950,000" in cleaned

    def test_allows_explicit_down_payment_from_evidence(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        candidates[0].metadata["down_payment"] = 500000

        text = """
A102 has a down payment of 500,000 EGP.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "500,000" in cleaned

    def test_does_not_allow_down_payment_from_another_property(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        candidates[0].metadata["down_payment"] = 500000

        text = """
A102 has a down payment of 500,000 EGP.
B205 has a down payment of 400,000 EGP.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102", "B205"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "500,000" in cleaned
        assert "400,000" not in cleaned

    def test_payment_plan_description_is_allowed(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
A102 has an installment payment plan.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "installment payment plan" in cleaned

    def test_unsupported_installment_amount_is_removed(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
A102 has monthly installments of 50,000 EGP.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "50,000" not in cleaned

    def test_unsupported_fee_statement_is_removed(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
A102 has administrative fees.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "administrative fees" not in cleaned

    def test_unsupported_discount_statement_is_removed(
        self,
        candidates,
    ):
        text = """
A102 has a special discount.

{"cited_property_ids": ["A102"]}
"""

        cleaned = generation._remove_unsupported_financial_claims(
            text,
            candidates,
        )

        assert "special discount" not in cleaned

import pytest
from importlib import import_module
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from app.rag.retrieval.hybrid_search import (
    hybrid_search,
    _min_max_normalize,
    _bm25_search,
    _qdrant_search,
    SearchResult,
)
from app.rag.retrieval.metadata_filter import MetadataFilter

def test_min_max_normalize():
    # Standard case
    assert _min_max_normalize([10, 20, 30]) == [0.0, 0.5, 1.0]

    # Empty case
    assert _min_max_normalize([]) == []

    # All same values
    assert _min_max_normalize([10, 10, 10]) == [1.0, 1.0, 1.0]


def test_bm25_search_basic():
    corpus = [
        {
            "chunk_id": "1",
            "text": "luxury apartment in New Cairo",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "2",
            "text": "cheap studio in Zayed",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "3",
            "text": "modern villa with pool",
        },
    ]

    # Search for "Cairo" - should match chunk 1
    results = _bm25_search("Cairo", corpus, top_k=1)
    chunk_ids = [r.chunk_id for r in results]

    assert chunk_ids == ["1"]
    assert "2" not in chunk_ids
    assert "3" not in chunk_ids
    assert results[0].lexical_score > 0


def test_bm25_search_preserves_source_file():
    corpus = [
        {
            "chunk_id": "1",
            "text": "luxury apartment in New Cairo",
            "file_name": "properties.csv",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "2",
            "text": "villa with swimming pool in Sheikh Zayed",
            "file_name": "villas.csv",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "3",
            "text": "modern apartment in Maadi",
            "file_name": "apartments.csv",
        },
    ]

    results = _bm25_search("Cairo", corpus, top_k=2)

    assert len(results) >= 1

    cairo_result = next(
        result
        for result in results
        if result.chunk_id == "1"
    )

    assert cairo_result.source_file == "properties.csv"


def test_qdrant_search_preserves_source_file():
    mock_client = MagicMock()

    mock_point = MagicMock()
    mock_point.payload = {
        "property_id": "p1",
        "chunk_id": "c1",
        "text": "villa in Sheikh Zayed",
        "file_name": "properties.csv",
        "source_path": "data/raw/properties/properties.csv",
    }
    mock_point.score = 0.95

    mock_client.search.return_value = [mock_point]

    # Empty MetadataFilter should produce no Qdrant filter.
    filt = MetadataFilter()

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.hybrid_search.embed_query",
        return_value=[0.1, 0.2, 0.3],
    ):
        results = _qdrant_search(
            "villa in Sheikh Zayed",
            filt,
            "realEstate",
            mock_client,
            top_k=1,
        )

    assert len(results) == 1
    assert results[0].property_id == "p1"
    assert results[0].chunk_id == "c1"
    assert results[0].source_file == "properties.csv"


def test_hybrid_search_semantic_only():
    # Mock qdrant_client and the internal search function
    mock_client = MagicMock()
    filt = MetadataFilter()

    mock_results = [
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p1",
            chunk_id="c1",
            text="text1",
            metadata={},
            semantic_score=0.9,
        ),
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p2",
            chunk_id="c2",
            text="text2",
            metadata={},
            semantic_score=0.7,
        ),
    ]

    with patch("app.rag.retrieval.hybrid_search._qdrant_search", return_value=mock_results):
        # corpus_chunks=None triggers semantic-only path
        results = hybrid_search(
            "query",
            filt,
            "coll",
            mock_client,
            corpus_chunks=None,
        )

        assert len(results) == 2
        assert results[0].chunk_id == "c1"

        # Raw semantic score is preserved;
        # combined_score is min-max normalized.
        assert results[0].semantic_score == 0.9
        assert results[0].combined_score == pytest.approx(1.0)


def test_hybrid_search_combined():
    mock_client = MagicMock()
    filt = MetadataFilter()

    # Semantic results
    semantic_results = [
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p1",
            chunk_id="c1",
            text="Cairo apartment",
            metadata={},
            semantic_score=0.8,
        ),
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p2",
            chunk_id="c2",
            text="Zayed villa",
            metadata={},
            semantic_score=0.6,
        ),
    ]

    # Lexical corpus
    corpus = [
        {
            "chunk_id": "c1",
            "text": "Cairo apartment",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "c2",
            "text": "Zayed villa",
        },
        {
            "chunk_id": "c3",
            "text": "Cairo luxury",
        },  # lexical hit only
    ]

    with patch("app.rag.retrieval.hybrid_search._qdrant_search", return_value=semantic_results):
        # Search for "Cairo"
        results = hybrid_search(
            "Cairo",
            filt,
            "coll",
            mock_client,
            corpus_chunks=corpus,
        )

        # c1 should be top because it's in both
        assert results[0].chunk_id == "c1"

        # c3 should be present because it's a lexical hit
        chunk_ids = [r.chunk_id for r in results]
        assert "c3" in chunk_ids

import pytest
from app.rag.retrieval.metadata_filter import (
    build_metadata_filter,
    matches,
    MetadataFilter,
    RangeConstraint,
    EqualityConstraint
)

def test_build_metadata_filter_basic():
    requirements = {
        "location": "New Cairo",
        "bedrooms": 3,
        "max_price": 5000000,
    }
    filt = build_metadata_filter(requirements, always_available_only=False)

    # Check equality
    eq_fields = [c.field for c in filt.equality]
    assert "location" in eq_fields
    assert "bedrooms" in eq_fields

    # Check ranges
    range_fields = [r.field for r in filt.ranges]
    assert "price" in range_fields
    assert filt.ranges[0].lte == 5000000

def test_build_metadata_filter_availability():
    requirements = {}
    filt = build_metadata_filter(requirements, always_available_only=True)

    # Should add availability == available by default
    assert any(c.field == "availability" and c.value == "available" for c in filt.equality)

def test_matches_success():
    property_metadata = {
        "location": "New Cairo",
        "bedrooms": 3,
        "price": 4000000,
        "availability": "available"
    }
    filt = MetadataFilter(
        equality=[EqualityConstraint(field="location", value="New Cairo")],
        ranges=[RangeConstraint(field="price", lte=5000000)]
    )
    assert matches(property_metadata, filt) is True

def test_matches_fail_equality():
    property_metadata = {
        "location": "Sheikh Zayed",
        "bedrooms": 3,
    }
    filt = MetadataFilter(
        equality=[EqualityConstraint(field="location", value="New Cairo")],
    )
    assert matches(property_metadata, filt) is False

def test_matches_fail_range():
    property_metadata = {
        "price": 6000000,
    }
    filt = MetadataFilter(
        ranges=[RangeConstraint(field="price", lte=5000000)],
    )
    assert matches(property_metadata, filt) is False

def test_matches_missing_field():
    property_metadata = {
        "location": "New Cairo",
    }
    filt = MetadataFilter(
        ranges=[RangeConstraint(field="price", lte=5000000)],
    )
    # If field is missing, it should not match
    assert matches(property_metadata, filt) is False

import pytest
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

from app.rag.retrieval.reranker import rerank, rerank_with_trace
from app.rag.retrieval.hybrid_search import SearchResult


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def local_cross_encoder_backend(settings_env):
    """These tests cover the cross-encoder path; the default backend is Groq."""
    settings_env(RERANKER_BACKEND="local")


@pytest.fixture
def candidates():
    return [
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p1",
            chunk_id="c1",
            text="High relevance text",
            metadata={"category": "villa"},
            combined_score=0.5,
            source_file="properties.csv",
        ),
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p2",
            chunk_id="c2",
            text="Medium relevance text",
            metadata={"category": "apartment"},
            combined_score=0.4,
            source_file="properties.csv",
        ),
        SearchResult(
            property_id="p3",
            chunk_id="c3",
            text="Low relevance text",
            metadata={"category": "villa"},
            combined_score=0.3,
            source_file="properties.csv",
        ),
    ]


def test_rerank_sorting(candidates):
    """Results should be sorted by cross-encoder score."""
    mock_scores = [0.1, 0.2, 0.9]

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()
        mock_model.predict.return_value = mock_scores
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        results = rerank("query", candidates, top_k=2)

    assert len(results) == 2

    assert results[0].chunk_id == "c3"
    assert results[0].combined_score == 0.9

    assert results[1].chunk_id == "c2"
    assert results[1].combined_score == 0.2


def test_rerank_preserves_original_score_in_metadata(candidates):
    """The original hybrid score should remain available for traceability."""
    mock_scores = [0.1, 0.2, 0.9]

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()
        mock_model.predict.return_value = mock_scores
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        results = rerank("query", candidates, top_k=3)

    result_by_chunk = {
        result.chunk_id: result
        for result in results
    }

    assert result_by_chunk["c1"].metadata["pre_rerank_score"] == 0.5
    assert result_by_chunk["c1"].metadata["rerank_score"] == 0.1

    assert result_by_chunk["c2"].metadata["pre_rerank_score"] == 0.4
    assert result_by_chunk["c2"].metadata["rerank_score"] == 0.2

    assert result_by_chunk["c3"].metadata["pre_rerank_score"] == 0.3
    assert result_by_chunk["c3"].metadata["rerank_score"] == 0.9


def test_rerank_preserves_source_file(candidates):
    """Reranking must not lose source traceability."""
    mock_scores = [0.1, 0.2, 0.9]

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()
        mock_model.predict.return_value = mock_scores
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        results = rerank("query", candidates, top_k=3)

    assert all(
        result.source_file == "properties.csv"
        for result in results
    )


def test_rerank_does_not_mutate_original_candidates(candidates):
    """Reranking should return replaced SearchResult objects."""
    original_scores = [
        candidate.combined_score
        for candidate in candidates
    ]

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()
        mock_model.predict.return_value = [0.1, 0.2, 0.9]
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        results = rerank("query", candidates, top_k=3)

    assert [candidate.combined_score for candidate in candidates] == original_scores
    assert results[0] is not candidates[2]


def test_rerank_empty():
    assert rerank("query", [], top_k=5) == []


def test_rerank_empty_query():
    assert rerank("", [], top_k=5) == []
    assert rerank("   ", [], top_k=5) == []


def test_rerank_non_string_query():
    assert rerank(None, [], top_k=5) == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize("top_k", [0, -1, -10])
def test_rerank_invalid_top_k(candidates, top_k):
    assert rerank("query", candidates, top_k=top_k) == []


def test_rerank_does_not_load_model_for_invalid_input():
    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        assert rerank("", [], top_k=5) == []
        assert rerank("query", [], top_k=5) == []
        assert rerank("query", [], top_k=0) == []

        mock_get.assert_not_called()


def test_rerank_raises_on_score_count_mismatch(candidates):
    """A model returning the wrong number of scores is a runtime error."""
    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()

        # Only two scores for three candidates.
        mock_model.predict.return_value = [0.1, 0.9]
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        with pytest.raises(
            RuntimeError,
            match="Reranker output count does not match candidate count",
        ):
            rerank("query", candidates, top_k=3)


def test_rerank_with_trace(candidates):
    mock_scores = [0.1, 0.2, 0.9]

    with patch(
        "app.rag.retrieval.reranker._get_reranker"
    ) as mock_get:
        mock_model = MagicMock()
        mock_model.predict.return_value = mock_scores
        mock_get.return_value = mock_model

        trace = rerank_with_trace(
            "query",
            candidates,
            top_k=2,
        )

    assert len(trace) == 2

    assert trace[0]["chunk_id"] == "c3"
    assert trace[0]["rerank_score"] == 0.9
    assert trace[0]["pre_rerank_score"] == 0.3
    assert trace[0]["source_file"] == "properties.csv"

    assert trace[1]["chunk_id"] == "c2"
    assert trace[1]["rerank_score"] == 0.2
    assert trace[1]["pre_rerank_score"] == 0.4
    assert trace[1]["source_file"] == "properties.csv"


def test_rerank_with_trace_empty():
    assert rerank_with_trace("query", [], top_k=5) == []


def test_rerank_with_trace_invalid_input(candidates):
    assert rerank_with_trace("", candidates, top_k=5) == []
    assert rerank_with_trace("   ", candidates, top_k=5) == []
    assert rerank_with_trace(None, candidates, top_k=5) == []

    assert rerank_with_trace("query", candidates, top_k=0) == []
    assert rerank_with_trace("query", candidates, top_k=-1) == []


def test_rerank_with_trace_raises_on_score_count_mismatch(candidates):

"""The static-site build for Cloudflare Pages / Vercel (scripts/build_frontend.py)."""

import importlib.util
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("build_frontend", ROOT / "scripts" / "build_frontend.py")
build_frontend = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules["build_frontend"] = build_frontend
spec.loader.exec_module(build_frontend)

API = "https://aqar-api.onrender.com"


@pytest.fixture
def built(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "dist"
    config = build_frontend.build(out, {"API_BASE_URL": API})
    return out, config


def test_files_are_laid_out_the_way_index_html_expects(built):
    out, _ = built
    html = (out / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for reference in re.findall(r'(?:src|href)="(/assets/[^"]+)"', html):
        assert (out / reference.lstrip("/")).exists(), reference
    assert (out / "assets" / "chat" / "voice-worklet.js").exists()  # loaded relative to voice.js
    assert (out / "_headers").exists()
    assert not (out / "assets" / "index.html").exists()


def test_runtime_config_points_the_site_at_the_api_and_hides_sample_listings(built):
    out, config = built
    js = (out / "assets" / "runtime-config.js").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    parsed = json.loads(js.split("window.APP_CONFIG = ", 1)[1].rstrip().rstrip(";"))
    assert parsed == config
    assert parsed["API_BASE_URL"] == API
    assert parsed["SHOW_PREVIEW_INVENTORY"] is False  # production never shows invented listings
    assert parsed["CHAT_DEFAULT_LANG"] == "ar" and parsed["VOICE_ENABLED"] is True


def test_the_csp_allows_only_self_and_the_api(built):
    out, _ = built
    csp = re.search(r"Content-Security-Policy: (.+)", (out / "_headers").read_text(encoding="utf-8")).group(1)
    assert "script-src 'self'" in csp and "'unsafe-eval'" not in csp
    assert "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'" not in csp  # inline scripts stay blocked: the XSS safety net
    assert f"connect-src 'self' {API} wss://aqar-api.onrender.com" in csp
    assert "object-src 'none'" in csp and "frame-ancestors 'none'" in csp and "base-uri 'none'" in csp
    # The brand fonts load from Google Fonts: allowed precisely, not via a blanket https: for styles/fonts.
    assert "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com" in csp
    assert "font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com" in csp
    assert "worklet-src" not in csp  # not a directive Chrome implements: it only logs an error
    html = (out / "index.html").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    assert 'http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy"' in html  # also delivered as <meta> for hosts that ignore _headers


def test_headers_file_has_the_hardening_headers_and_short_cache_rules(built):
    headers = (built[0] / "_headers").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    for expected in ("X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff", "X-Frame-Options: DENY", "Strict-Transport-Security:", "microphone=(self)",
                     "/assets/runtime-config.js\n  Cache-Control: no-cache"):
        assert expected in headers


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("value", "message"),
    [
        (None, "required"),
        ("", "required"),
        ("not a url", "absolute"),
        ("ftp://api.example.com", "absolute"),
        ("http://api.example.com", "https"),
        ("https://api.example.com/v1", "origin only"),
        ("https://api.example.com/?x=1", "origin only"),
    ],
)
def test_a_wrong_api_url_fails_the_build_instead_of_shipping_a_broken_site(tmp_path, value, message):
    with pytest.raises(build_frontend.BuildError, match=message):
        build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "dist", {"API_BASE_URL": value} if value is not None else {})


def test_local_http_api_is_allowed_only_for_localhost(tmp_path):
    build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "a", {"API_BASE_URL": "http://localhost:8000"})
    with pytest.raises(build_frontend.BuildError):
        build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "b", {"API_BASE_URL": "http://192.168.1.5:8000"})
    build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "c", {"API_BASE_URL": "http://192.168.1.5:8000"}, allow_insecure=True)


def test_trailing_slash_is_normalised(tmp_path):
    assert build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "d", {"API_BASE_URL": API + "/"})["API_BASE_URL"] == API


def test_other_options_are_validated(tmp_path):
    with pytest.raises(build_frontend.BuildError):
        build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "e", {"API_BASE_URL": API, "CHAT_DEFAULT_LANG": "fr"})
    with pytest.raises(build_frontend.BuildError):
        build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "f", {"API_BASE_URL": API, "VOICE_ENABLED": "maybe"})
    config = build_frontend.build(tmp_path / "g", {"API_BASE_URL": API, "VOICE_ENABLED": "false", "CHAT_DEFAULT_LANG": "en",
                                                   "REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS": "90000", "SHOW_PREVIEW_INVENTORY": "true"})
    assert (config["VOICE_ENABLED"], config["CHAT_DEFAULT_LANG"], config["REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS"], config["SHOW_PREVIEW_INVENTORY"]) == (False, "en", 90000, True)


def test_config_values_cannot_break_out_of_the_script(tmp_path):
    js = build_frontend.runtime_config_js({"API_BASE_URL": 'https://x.example"</script><script>alert(1)//'})
    assert "</script>" not in js  # JSON-escaped, so a hostile value cannot inject markup


def test_a_rebuild_replaces_the_previous_output(tmp_path):
    out = tmp_path / "dist"
    build_frontend.build(out, {"API_BASE_URL": API})
    (out / "stale.txt").write_text("old")
    build_frontend.build(out, {"API_BASE_URL": API})
    assert not (out / "stale.txt").exists()


def test_the_site_source_never_contains_credentials_or_the_real_api_url():
    leaks = []
    pattern = re.compile(r"(AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{20,}|gsk_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}|EAA[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|onrender\.com|neon\.tech|qdrant\.io)")
    for path in (ROOT / "app" / "frontend").rglob("*"):
        if path.is_file() and path.suffix in {".js", ".html", ".css"}:
            leaks += [f"{path.name}: {m}" for m in pattern.findall(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    assert leaks == []


def test_sample_listings_on_a_real_site_trigger_a_loud_build_warning():
    on = build_frontend.build_config({"SHOW_PREVIEW_INVENTORY": "true"}, API)
    off = build_frontend.build_config({}, API)
    local = build_frontend.build_config({"SHOW_PREVIEW_INVENTORY": "true"}, "http://127.0.0.1:8000")

    assert "INVENTED sample listings" in build_frontend.sample_inventory_warning(on)
    assert build_frontend.sample_inventory_warning(off) is None
    assert build_frontend.sample_inventory_warning(local) is None

"""Production configuration is validated before the app serves a single request."""

import pytest

from app.helpers.config import Settings

GOOD = dict(
    APP_ENV="production",
    DATABASE_URL="postgresql://u:p@ep-x.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech/db?sslmode=require",
    SESSION_SECRET="s" * 40,
    ADMIN_API_KEY="a" * 30,
    CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS="https://app.example.com",
    GROQ_API_KEY="gsk_x",
    GEMINI_API_KEY="AIza_x",
    QDRANT_URL="https://abc.eu-central.aws.cloud.qdrant.io:6333",
    QDRANT_API_KEY="qk",
    TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1,
    RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=True,
)


def make(**overrides) -> Settings:
    # Explicit None must stay explicit: it overrides the variables conftest exports,
    # otherwise a "missing" setting would silently be picked up from the environment.
    return Settings(_env_file=None, **{**GOOD, **overrides})


def test_a_complete_production_configuration_has_no_problems():
    assert make().production_problems() == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("override", "fragment"),
    [
        ({"DATABASE_URL": None}, "DATABASE_URL"),
        ({"SESSION_SECRET": "short"}, "SESSION_SECRET"),
        ({"SESSION_SECRET": None}, "SESSION_SECRET"),
        ({"ADMIN_API_KEY": "tooshort"}, "ADMIN_API_KEY"),
        ({"ADMIN_API_KEY": None}, "ADMIN_API_KEY"),
        ({"CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "*"}, "CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS"),
        ({"CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "http://app.example.com"}, "must use https"),
        ({"CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS": "https://a.example.com,*"}, "CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS"),
        ({"GROQ_API_KEY": None}, "GROQ_API_KEY"),
        ({"GEMINI_API_KEY": None}, "GEMINI_API_KEY"),
        ({"QDRANT_URL": "http://localhost:6333"}, "QDRANT_URL"),
        ({"QDRANT_URL": None}, "QDRANT_URL"),
        ({"QDRANT_API_KEY": None}, "QDRANT_API_KEY"),
        ({"TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS": 0}, "TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS"),
        ({"WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN": "t"}, "WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET"),  # a half-configured channel is an error
    ],
)
def test_each_missing_or_unsafe_setting_is_reported(override, fragment):
    problems = make(**override).production_problems()
    assert any(fragment in problem for problem in problems), problems


def test_problems_never_contain_secret_values():
    settings = make(SESSION_SECRET="short-secret-value", ADMIN_API_KEY="short-admin-value", GROQ_API_KEY=None)
    text = " ".join(settings.production_problems())
    assert "short-secret-value" not in text and "short-admin-value" not in text


def test_gemini_key_is_not_required_when_embeddings_run_locally():
    assert make(GEMINI_API_KEY=None, EMBEDDING_BACKEND="local").production_problems() == []


def test_local_origins_are_fine_in_development_but_flagged_for_production():
    assert Settings(_env_file=None, APP_ENV="development").is_production is False
    assert make(CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS="http://localhost:3000").production_problems() == []  # localhost is exempt from https


def test_pasted_quotes_and_whitespace_are_stripped_from_secrets():
    # Hosting dashboards make a trailing newline or quotes easy to paste.
    settings = make(GROQ_API_KEY='  "gsk_abc"\n', SESSION_SECRET=" " + "s" * 40 + " ")
    assert settings.GROQ_API_KEY == "gsk_abc"
    assert settings.SESSION_SECRET == "s" * 40


def test_blank_optional_values_count_as_unset():
    settings = make(DATABASE_URL="", FILE_MAX_SIZE="", POSTGRES_PORT="", ENABLE_API_DOCS="")
    assert settings.DATABASE_URL is None and settings.FILE_MAX_SIZE is None and settings.ENABLE_API_DOCS is None


def test_docs_and_metrics_are_closed_in_production_and_open_in_development():
    assert make().docs_enabled is False and make().metrics_public is False
    dev = Settings(_env_file=None, APP_ENV="development")
    assert dev.docs_enabled is True and dev.metrics_public is True
    assert make(ENABLE_API_DOCS="true").docs_enabled is True  # explicit opt-in wins


def test_staff_channels_are_detected_from_complete_settings_only():
    assert make().staff_channels == []
    assert make(TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="t").staff_channels == []  # chat id missing
    assert make(TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN="t", TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID="1", STAFF_WEBHOOK_URL="https://hooks.example/x").staff_channels == [
        "webhook",
        "telegram",
    ]


def test_database_url_helpers_handle_neon_and_special_characters():
    from sqlalchemy.engine import make_url

    from app.database import url as urls

    neon = make(DATABASE_URL="postgres://user:p%40ss%2Fw@ep-1.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech/neondb")
    sync = urls.sync_url(neon)
    assert sync.drivername == "postgresql+psycopg"
    assert sync.password == "p@ss/w"
    assert sync.query["sslmode"] == "require"  # remote hosts always get TLS

    async_url = urls.async_url(neon)
    assert async_url.drivername == "postgresql+asyncpg" and async_url.query["ssl"] == "require"
    assert "sslmode" not in async_url.query  # asyncpg would reject it

    local = urls.sync_url(make(DATABASE_URL="postgresql://u:p@localhost:5432/db"))
    assert "sslmode" not in local.query

    parts = make(DATABASE_URL=None, POSTGRES_HOST="db.internal", POSTGRES_USERNAME="u", POSTGRES_PASSWORD="p@ss:w/rd",
                 POSTGRES_PORT="5432", POSTGRES_MAIN_DATABASE="app")
    built = urls.sync_url(parts)
    assert make_url(built.render_as_string(hide_password=False)).password == "p@ss:w/rd"  # escaped, so it round-trips

    assert "secret" not in urls.redacted(make_url("postgresql://u:secret@h/db"))


def test_incomplete_postgres_parts_name_what_is_missing_without_values():
    from app.database import url as urls

    with pytest.raises(urls.DatabaseConfigError) as error:
        urls.sync_url(make(DATABASE_URL=None, POSTGRES_HOST="h", POSTGRES_PASSWORD="hunter2"))
    assert "POSTGRES_USERNAME" in str(error.value) and "hunter2" not in str(error.value)


def test_production_without_a_database_is_an_error_not_a_silent_sqlite_fallback():
    from app.database import url as urls

    with pytest.raises(urls.DatabaseConfigError):
        urls.resolve_url(make(DATABASE_URL=None))

"""Nothing credential-shaped may be committed, and the example env file must stay empty."""

import re
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]

# Shapes of real provider credentials (Groq, Google, Meta, OpenAI-style, AWS, Slack, GitHub, private keys).
SECRET_SHAPES = re.compile(
    r"(AIza[0-9A-Za-z_\-]{30,}|gsk_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|EAA[A-Za-z0-9]{40,}|sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{32,}|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}"
    r"|-----BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----|xox[abp]-[0-9A-Za-z-]{20,}|ghp_[A-Za-z0-9]{30,}"
    r"|postgres(?:ql)?(?:\+\w+)?://[^\s:@/<>]+:(?!password|pass|secret|\*|\[|<|\$)[^\s@/<>]{6,}@[a-z0-9.-]+\.(?:neon\.tech|aws|azure|amazonaws\.com))"
)
SCANNED_DIRS = ("app", "scripts", "alembic")
SCANNED_FILES = ("render.yaml", "Dockerfile", "docker-compose.yml", "vercel.json", ".env.example", "README.md", "alembic.ini")
SKIP_SUFFIXES = {".pyc", ".png", ".jpg", ".jpeg", ".docx", ".csv", ".sqlite3"}


def tracked_text_files():
    for name in SCANNED_FILES:
        path = ROOT / name
        if path.exists():
            yield path
    for directory in SCANNED_DIRS:
        for path in (ROOT / directory).rglob("*"):
            if path.is_file() and path.suffix not in SKIP_SUFFIXES and "__pycache__" not in path.parts:
                yield path


def test_no_file_contains_a_credential_shaped_string():
    leaks = []
    for path in tracked_text_files():
        try:
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue
        leaks += [f"{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: {match.group(0)[:12]}..." for match in SECRET_SHAPES.finditer(text)]
    assert leaks == []


def test_the_example_env_file_has_no_values_for_secret_settings():
    secret_names = (
        "SESSION_SECRET", "ADMIN_API_KEY", "DATABASE_URL", "POSTGRES_PASSWORD", "QDRANT_API_KEY", "GROQ_API_KEY",
        "GEMINI_API_KEY", "WHATSAPP_VERIFY_TOKEN", "WHATSAPP_APP_SECRET", "WHATSAPP_ACCESS_TOKEN", "WHATSAPP_GATEWAY_SECRET",
        "TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN", "SMTP_PASSWORD", "STAFF_WEBHOOK_URL",
    )
    values = dict(
        line.split("=", 1) for line in (ROOT / ".env.example").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        if "=" in line and not line.lstrip().startswith("#")
    )
    filled = {name: values[name] for name in secret_names if values.get(name, "").strip()}
    assert filled == {}


def test_real_env_files_are_git_ignored():
    ignore = (ROOT / ".gitignore").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert ".env" in ignore and ".env.*" in ignore and "!.env.example" in ignore


def test_the_docker_context_excludes_env_files_and_history():
    ignore = (ROOT / ".dockerignore").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert {".env", ".env.*", ".git"} <= set(ignore)


def test_the_detector_itself_recognises_real_looking_keys():
    fake_google = "AIza" + "SyD-9tSrke72PouQMnMX-a7eZSW0jkFMBWY"
    fake_groq = "gsk_" + "AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz0123"
    fake_dsn = "postgresql://owner:realpassword99@ep-cool-1.eu-central-1.aws.neon.tech/db"
    for sample in (fake_google, fake_groq, fake_dsn):
        assert SECRET_SHAPES.search(sample), sample
    for harmless in ("postgresql://user:password@localhost/db", "postgresql://aqar:aqar_test_pw@127.0.0.1:55432/aqar_test", "gsk_[A-Za-z0-9]{10,}"):
        assert not SECRET_SHAPES.search(harmless), harmless

from app.helpers.phone import display_phone, is_valid_phone, mask_phone, normalize_phone, spoken_phone


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

        "Û°Û±Û°Û±Û²Û³Û´ÛµÛ¶Û·Û¸",  # Persian digits

def test_egyptian_mobile_formats_normalize_to_one_e164_string(raw):

@pytest.mark.parametrize("prefix", ["010", "011", "012", "015"])
def test_every_egyptian_operator_prefix_is_accepted(prefix):
    assert normalize_phone(f"{prefix}12345678") == f"+20{prefix[1:]}12345678"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "raw",
    [
        None,
        "",
        "   ",
        "abc",
        "0101234",  # too short
        "010123456789",  # too long for a local number
        "01312345678",  # 013 is not an operator prefix
        "02 2345 6789",  # a landline cannot be reached by WhatsApp or an advisor's mobile call list
        "0101abc5678",  # letters inside the number
        "+0101234567",
        "++201012345678",
        "20+1012345678",
        "+999",
        "123456789",  # a bare local number from an unknown country
        "+2001012345678",  # wrong digit count after +20
    ],
)
def test_invalid_numbers_are_rejected_not_guessed(raw):
    assert normalize_phone(raw) is None
    assert is_valid_phone(raw) is False


def test_international_numbers_need_an_explicit_country_code():
    assert normalize_phone("+447911123456") == "+447911123456"
    assert normalize_phone("00447911123456") == "+447911123456"
    assert normalize_phone("+1 (415) 555-2671") == "+14155552671"


def test_normalization_is_idempotent():
    once = normalize_phone("0101 234 5678")
    assert normalize_phone(once) == once


def test_masking_hides_the_middle_of_a_number_in_logs():
    masked = mask_phone("+201012345678")
    assert masked.startswith("+201") and masked.endswith("78")
    assert "1234567" not in masked
    assert mask_phone(None) == "***"
    assert mask_phone("123") == "***"


def test_readback_formats_are_unambiguous():
    assert display_phone("+201012345678") == "0101 234 5678"
    # Voice reads digit by digit so speech can never merge or reorder them.
    assert spoken_phone("+201012345678") == "0 1 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8"
    assert spoken_phone("+447911123456") == "4 4 7 9 1 1 1 2 3 4 5 6"

def test_detect_file_type():
    assert detect_file_type("property.pdf") == "pdf"
    assert detect_file_type("property.docx") == "office"
    assert detect_file_type("property.pptx") == "office"
    assert detect_file_type("property.txt") == "text"
    assert detect_file_type("property.md") == "text"
    assert detect_file_type("properties.csv") == "spreadsheet"
    assert detect_file_type("properties.xlsx") == "spreadsheet"
    assert detect_file_type("property.jpg") == "image"


def test_is_supported():
    assert is_supported("property.pdf")
    assert is_supported("property.docx")
    assert is_supported("property.txt")
    assert is_supported("properties.xlsx")
    assert is_supported("property.jpg")

    assert not is_supported("property.exe")


def test_ingest_text_file(tmp_path: Path):
    file_path = tmp_path / "property.txt"

    file_path.write_text(
        """
        Property: Mountain View
        Location: New Cairo
        Type: Apartment
        Bedrooms: 3
        Bathrooms: 2
        Area: 180 sqm
        Price: 5,000,000 EGP

        The apartment has a garden view and is located
        near the main entrance of the compound.
        """,
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    result = ingest_file(
        str(file_path),
        property_id="PROP-001",
    )

    assert result["status"] == "success"
    assert result["file_type"] == "text"
    assert result["chunks_count"] > 0

    chunks = result["chunks"]

    assert len(chunks) > 0

    first_chunk = chunks[0]

    assert "id" in first_chunk
    assert "text" in first_chunk
    assert "metadata" in first_chunk

    assert first_chunk["metadata"]["property_id"] == "PROP-001"
    assert first_chunk["metadata"]["source"] == "property.txt"


def test_ingest_empty_text_file(tmp_path: Path):
    file_path = tmp_path / "empty.txt"

    file_path.write_text(
        "",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    result = ingest_file(str(file_path))

    assert result["status"] == "empty"


def test_ingest_unsupported_file(tmp_path: Path):
    file_path = tmp_path / "property.exe"

    file_path.write_text(
        "fake content",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    result = ingest_file(str(file_path))

    assert result["status"] == "unsupported"

"""Rate limiting, client identification, session/token signing and log redaction."""

import json
import logging
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest
from fastapi import HTTPException

from app.api import ratelimit
from app.api.ratelimit import SlidingWindowLimiter, client_ip
from app.api import sessions
from app.observability.logging import JsonFormatter, RedactingFilter, redact


def request(peer="10.1.1.1", forwarded=None):
    headers = {"x-forwarded-for": forwarded} if forwarded else {}
    return SimpleNamespace(headers=headers, client=SimpleNamespace(host=peer), url=SimpleNamespace(path="/x"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sliding window
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_window_allows_up_to_the_limit_then_reports_when_to_retry():
    limiter = SlidingWindowLimiter()
    assert [limiter.hit("k", 3, 60) for _ in range(3)] == [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    retry = limiter.hit("k", 3, 60)
    assert 0 < retry <= 60
    assert limiter.hit("other", 3, 60) == 0.0  # keys are independent


def test_window_slides_instead_of_resetting_in_blocks(monkeypatch):
    limiter = SlidingWindowLimiter()
    now = [1000.0]
    monkeypatch.setattr(time, "monotonic", lambda: now[0])
    assert limiter.hit("k", 2, 10) == 0 and limiter.hit("k", 2, 10) == 0
    now[0] += 9
    assert limiter.hit("k", 2, 10) > 0  # still full
    now[0] += 1.5
    assert limiter.hit("k", 2, 10) == 0  # the first hit aged out


def test_memory_is_bounded_when_an_attacker_rotates_identities(monkeypatch):
    limiter = SlidingWindowLimiter(max_keys=50)
    for index in range(500):
        limiter.hit(f"ip-{index}", 5, 60)
    assert len(limiter._hits) <= 50 + 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Client identity
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_without_a_trusted_proxy_forwarded_headers_are_ignored(settings_env):
    settings_env(TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS="0")
    assert client_ip(request(peer="10.1.1.1", forwarded="6.6.6.6")) == "10.1.1.1"


def test_behind_one_proxy_the_rightmost_entry_is_the_client_and_forged_ones_are_ignored(settings_env):
    settings_env(TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS="1")
    honest = client_ip(request(forwarded="203.0.113.5"))
    spoofed = client_ip(request(forwarded="1.1.1.1, 2.2.2.2, 203.0.113.5"))
    assert honest == spoofed == "203.0.113.5"  # prepending fake hops buys an attacker nothing


def test_two_trusted_proxies_pick_the_entry_before_the_last(settings_env):
    settings_env(TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS="2")
    assert client_ip(request(forwarded="9.9.9.9, 203.0.113.5, 198.51.100.1")) == "203.0.113.5"


def test_a_short_header_falls_back_safely_and_garbage_cannot_blow_up(settings_env):
    settings_env(TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS="3")
    assert client_ip(request(forwarded="203.0.113.5")) == "203.0.113.5"
    assert client_ip(request(forwarded="x" * 500)) == "x" * 64  # truncated, never unbounded
    assert client_ip(SimpleNamespace(headers={}, client=None)) == "unknown"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enforcement
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_exceeding_a_limit_raises_429_with_retry_after(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_SEARCH_PER_MINUTE="2")
    ratelimit.limit_search(request())
    ratelimit.limit_search(request())
    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as error:
        ratelimit.limit_search(request())
    assert error.value.status_code == 429
    assert int(error.value.headers["Retry-After"]) >= 1
    ratelimit.limit_search(request(peer="10.9.9.9"))  # another client is unaffected


def test_disabled_limiting_never_blocks(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="false", RATE_LIMIT_SEARCH_PER_MINUTE="1")
    for _ in range(20):
        ratelimit.limit_search(request())


def test_chat_is_limited_per_ip_and_per_session(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_PER_MINUTE="100", RATE_LIMIT_CHAT_SESSION_PER_MINUTE="2")
    ratelimit.limit_chat(request(), "session-a")
    ratelimit.limit_chat(request(), "session-a")
    with pytest.raises(HTTPException):
        ratelimit.limit_chat(request(), "session-a")  # one chatty session
    ratelimit.limit_chat(request(), "session-b")  # a different session from the same IP is fine


def test_voice_tokens_are_limited_per_ip_and_per_session(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_VOICE_TOKEN_PER_MINUTE="2")
    ratelimit.limit_voice_token(request(), "s1")
    ratelimit.limit_voice_token(request(), "s1")
    with pytest.raises(HTTPException):
        ratelimit.limit_voice_token(request(), "s1")


def test_repeated_wrong_admin_keys_lock_the_client_out_even_for_the_right_key(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN_FAILURES_PER_15MIN="3", RATE_LIMIT_ADMIN_PER_MINUTE="1000")
    attacker = request(peer="10.6.6.6")
    for _ in range(3):
        ratelimit.limit_admin(attacker)
        ratelimit.record_admin_failure(attacker)
    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as error:
        ratelimit.limit_admin(attacker)
    assert error.value.status_code == 429
    ratelimit.limit_admin(request(peer="10.7.7.7"))  # the operator on another address still works


def test_whatsapp_flood_is_dropped_per_sender(settings_env):
    settings_env(RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED="true", RATE_LIMIT_WHATSAPP_SENDER_PER_MINUTE="3")
    assert [ratelimit.allow_whatsapp_sender("2010") for _ in range(5)] == [True, True, True, False, False]
    assert ratelimit.allow_whatsapp_sender("2011") is True

def test_session_ids_verify_and_survive_resigning():
    session_id = sessions.issue_session_id()
    raw = sessions.verify_session_id(session_id)
    assert raw and sessions.website_thread(raw) == f"web:{raw}"
    refreshed = sessions.issue_session_id(raw)
    assert sessions.verify_session_id(refreshed) == raw  # same conversation, fresh timestamp


@pytest.mark.parametrize("mutate", [
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: f"{raw}x.{stamp}.{sig}",          # different conversation, old signature
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: f"{raw}.{stamp}0.{sig}",          # forged timestamp
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: f"{raw}.{stamp}.{sig[:-1]}{'1' if sig[-1] == '0' else '0'}",  # corrupted signature (always differs)
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: f"{raw}.{stamp}",                 # old two-part format
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: f"{raw}.{stamp}.{sig}.extra",
    lambda raw, stamp, sig: "",
])
def test_tampered_session_ids_are_rejected(mutate):
    raw, stamp, sig = sessions.issue_session_id().split(".")
    assert sessions.verify_session_id(mutate(raw, stamp, sig)) is None


def test_session_ids_expire_and_report_when_to_refresh(settings_env):
    settings_env(SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS="30")
    long_ago = time.time() - 31 * 86400
    assert sessions.verify_session_id(sessions.issue_session_id(now=long_ago)) is None
    old_but_valid = sessions.issue_session_id(now=time.time() - 3 * 86400)
    raw, age = sessions.inspect_session_id(old_but_valid)
    assert raw and sessions.needs_refresh(age)
    assert not sessions.needs_refresh(sessions.inspect_session_id(sessions.issue_session_id())[1])
    assert sessions.verify_session_id(sessions.issue_session_id(now=time.time() + 3600)) is None  # from the future


def test_a_different_server_secret_invalidates_every_session(settings_env):
    session_id = sessions.issue_session_id()
    settings_env(SESSION_SECRET="another-secret-0123456789abcdef0123456789")
    sessions.reset_secret_cache()
    assert sessions.verify_session_id(session_id) is None


def test_voice_tokens_expire_and_only_work_once():
    token = sessions.issue_voice_token("raw-session", "ar")
    claims = sessions.consume_voice_token(token)
    assert claims and claims["sid"] == "raw-session" and claims["lang"] == "ar"
    assert sessions.consume_voice_token(token) is None  # replay


def test_expired_and_forged_voice_tokens_are_rejected(settings_env):
    settings_env(VOICE_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS="-5")
    assert sessions.consume_voice_token(sessions.issue_voice_token("s", "en")) is None
    settings_env(VOICE_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS="60")
    token = sessions.issue_voice_token("s", "en")
    body, signature = token.split(".")
    assert sessions.verify_voice_token(f"{body}.{'0' * len(signature)}") is None
    assert sessions.verify_voice_token(None) is None
    assert sessions.verify_voice_token("x" * 600) is None


def test_voice_token_language_is_restricted():
    claims = sessions.verify_voice_token(sessions.issue_voice_token("s", "fr"))
    assert claims["lang"] == "en"


def test_origin_check_allows_listed_origins_only(settings_env):
    settings_env(CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS="https://app.example.com,https://www.example.com/")
    assert sessions.origin_allowed("https://app.example.com")
    assert sessions.origin_allowed("https://www.example.com/")
    assert not sessions.origin_allowed("https://evil.example")
    assert not sessions.origin_allowed(None)  # browsers always send Origin on WebSocket handshakes
    settings_env(CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS="*")
    assert sessions.origin_allowed(None)
